In my previous reply, removing pub type_: String from RoomRegistered and SiblingDeclared would have violated the requirement in Step 1 that hash::hash_of and hash::body_for_signing on a bare RoomRegistered or SiblingDeclared struct must still include its "type" field.
Here is the corrected Step 1 implementation: RoomRegistered and SiblingDeclared retain their #[serde(rename = "type")] pub type_: String field so their standalone serialized form, hash, and signing body are completely unchanged, while CommonsRecord uses custom Serialize and Deserialize implementations (checking "type" on read and delegating directly to the inner struct on write) so that CommonsRecord writes "type" exactly once in JSON and round-trips cleanly.
src/commons.rs
use crate::did::{DidKey, Keypair};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::hash;
use crate::proof::{Proof, ProofOrArray};
use crate::room::Room;
use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CommonsLog {
    pub commons_id: DidKey,
    pub records: Vec<CommonsRecord>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RoomRegistered {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub type_: String,
    pub commons_id: DidKey,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub prev: Option<String>,
    pub room_id: DidKey,
    pub topic: String,
    pub template_hash: String,
    pub room_seed_hash: String,
    pub registered_by: DidKey,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub also_listed_in: Vec<DidKey>,
    pub ts: String,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SiblingDeclared {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub type_: String,
    pub commons_id: DidKey,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub prev: Option<String>,
    pub parent_id: DidKey,
    pub sibling_id: DidKey,
    pub parent_kw_id: DidKey,
    pub shard_hash: String,
    pub purpose: String,
    pub ts: String,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum CommonsRecord {
    RoomRegistered(RoomRegistered),
    SiblingDeclared(SiblingDeclared),
}

impl Serialize for CommonsRecord {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> std::result::Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => r.serialize(serializer),
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => s.serialize(serializer),
        }
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for CommonsRecord {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> std::result::Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let v = serde_json::Value::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let t = v
            .get("type")
            .and_then(|x| x.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| serde::de::Error::missing_field("type"))?;
        match t {
            "room_registered" => {
                let r: RoomRegistered =
                    serde_json::from_value(v).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?;
                Ok(CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r))
            }
            "sibling_declared" => {
                let s: SiblingDeclared =
                    serde_json::from_value(v).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?;
                Ok(CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s))
            }
            other => Err(serde::de::Error::unknown_variant(
                other,
                &["room_registered", "sibling_declared"],
            )),
        }
    }
}

impl CommonsRecord {
    pub fn hash(&self) -> Result<String> {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => hash::hash_of(r),
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => hash::hash_of(s),
        }
    }
    pub fn prev(&self) -> Option<&String> {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => r.prev.as_ref(),
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => s.prev.as_ref(),
        }
    }
    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => r.seq,
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => s.seq,
        }
    }
    pub fn proof(&self) -> &ProofOrArray {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => &r.proof,
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => &s.proof,
        }
    }
}

pub struct Commons {
    pub world_id: DidKey,
    keypair: Keypair,
    records: Vec<CommonsRecord>,
}

impl Commons {
    pub fn new(keypair: Keypair) -> Self {
        let world_id = keypair.did();
        Commons { world_id, keypair, records: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn records(&self) -> &[CommonsRecord] {
        &self.records
    }

    pub fn log(&self) -> CommonsLog {
        CommonsLog {
            commons_id: self.world_id.clone(),
            records: self.records.clone(),
        }
    }

    pub fn register_room(
        &mut self,
        room: &Room,
        registrant_kp: &Keypair,
        topic: Option<String>,
    ) -> Result<RoomRegistered> {
        let seq = self.records.len() as u64;
        let prev = match self.records.last() {
            Some(r) => Some(r.hash()?),
            None => None,
        };
        let seed_hash = room.records().first()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("room has no seed".into()))?
            .hash()?;
        let mut rec = RoomRegistered {
            type_: "room_registered".into(),
            commons_id: self.world_id.clone(),
            seq, prev,
            room_id: room.world_id().clone(),
            topic: topic.unwrap_or_else(|| room.template().topic.clone()),
            template_hash: room.template().hash()?,
            room_seed_hash: seed_hash,
            registered_by: registrant_kp.did(),
            also_listed_in: Vec::new(),
            ts: crate::now(),
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = hash::body_for_signing(&rec)?;
        let reg_sig = registrant_kp.sign(&body);
        let commons_sig = self.keypair.sign(&body);
        rec.proof = ProofOrArray::array(vec![
            Proof::create(registrant_kp, &reg_sig),
            Proof::create(&self.keypair, &commons_sig),
        ]);
        self.records.push(CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(rec.clone()));
        Ok(rec)
    }

    /// Record a sibling declaration in the Commons. Signed by
    /// parent + sibling + Commons. The shard_hash must name a
    /// KnowledgeShardExport record in the parent's KnowledgeWorld;
    /// the crate cannot verify that cross-reference (it's a
    /// reader-side check when both logs are available), so the
    /// hash is taken on faith here.
    pub fn declare_sibling(
        &mut self,
        parent_kp: &Keypair,
        sibling_kp: &Keypair,
        parent_kw_id: &DidKey,
        shard_hash: &str,
        purpose: &str,
    ) -> Result<SiblingDeclared> {
        if parent_kp.did() == sibling_kp.did() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("parent == sibling".into()));
        }
        if shard_hash.len() != 64 || !shard_hash.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("shard_hash must be 64 hex chars".into()));
        }
        let seq = self.records.len() as u64;
        let prev = match self.records.last() {
            Some(r) => Some(r.hash()?),
            None => None,
        };
        let mut rec = SiblingDeclared {
            type_: "sibling_declared".into(),
            commons_id: self.world_id.clone(),
            seq, prev,
            parent_id: parent_kp.did(),
            sibling_id: sibling_kp.did(),
            parent_kw_id: parent_kw_id.clone(),
            shard_hash: shard_hash.into(),
            purpose: purpose.into(),
            ts: crate::now(),
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = hash::body_for_signing(&rec)?;
        let p_sig = parent_kp.sign(&body);
        let s_sig = sibling_kp.sign(&body);
        let c_sig = self.keypair.sign(&body);
        rec.proof = ProofOrArray::array(vec![
            Proof::create(parent_kp, &p_sig),
            Proof::create(sibling_kp, &s_sig),
            Proof::create(&self.keypair, &c_sig),
        ]);
        self.records.push(CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(rec.clone()));
        Ok(rec)
    }
}

pub fn verify_commons(commons: &Commons) -> Result<()> {
    verify_commons_log(&commons.log())
}

pub fn verify_commons_log(log: &CommonsLog) -> Result<()> {
    let mut prev: Option<String> = None;
    for (i, rec) in log.records.iter().enumerate() {
        match rec {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => {
                if r.type_ != "room_registered" {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: bad type")));
                }
                if r.commons_id != log.commons_id {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: commons_id mismatch")));
                }
                if r.prev != prev {
                    return Err(Error::Chain(format!("record {i}: prev mismatch")));
                }
                let body = hash::body_for_signing(r)?;
                let reg = r.proof.find_by_method(&r.registered_by)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing registrant proof")))?;
                reg.verify(&body)?;
                let com = r.proof.find_by_method(&log.commons_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing commons proof")))?;
                com.verify(&body)?;
            }
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => {
                if s.type_ != "sibling_declared" {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: bad type")));
                }
                if s.commons_id != log.commons_id {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: commons_id mismatch")));
                }
                if s.prev != prev {
                    return Err(Error::Chain(format!("record {i}: prev mismatch")));
                }
                if s.parent_id == s.sibling_id {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!("record {i}: parent == sibling")));
                }
                if s.shard_hash.len() != 64 || !s.shard_hash.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!("record {i}: bad shard_hash")));
                }
                let body = hash::body_for_signing(s)?;
                let p = s.proof.find_by_method(&s.parent_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing parent proof")))?;
                p.verify(&body)?;
                let sib = s.proof.find_by_method(&s.sibling_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing sibling proof")))?;
                sib.verify(&body)?;
                let com = s.proof.find_by_method(&log.commons_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing commons proof")))?;
                com.verify(&body)?;
            }
        }
        prev = Some(rec.hash()?);
    }
    Ok(())
}

STEP 2 writes tests/commons_attack.rs to probe verify_commons_log against forged, reordered, and duplicate CommonsLog records.
1. Attack Inventory and Expected Outcomes
Every test takes an honest CommonsLog, modifies one thing, and asserts verify_commons_log(&log).is_err():
 * Proofs
   * attack_proofs_registration_without_commons_proof: PASS — verify_commons_log requires a proof from log.commons_id and refuses when only the registrant's proof is present.
   * attack_proofs_registration_without_registrant_proof: PASS — verify_commons_log requires a proof from r.registered_by and refuses when only the Commons' proof is present.
   * attack_proofs_moved_from_one_record_to_another: PASS — moving ProofOrArray from one registration to another with a different room_id/seq fails signature verification over body_for_signing.
   * attack_proofs_registration_signed_by_wrong_registrant_key: PASS — signing a registration with mallory's key while registered_by names alice fails r.proof.find_by_method(&r.registered_by).
   * attack_proofs_sibling_without_sibling_proof: PASS — verify_commons_log requires proofs from parent_id, sibling_id, and commons_id, and refuses when the sibling's proof is missing.
 * Order
   * attack_order_two_records_swapped: PASS — swapping two records breaks r.prev != prev.
   * attack_order_record_dropped_from_middle: PASS — removing the middle record of three breaks r.prev != prev on the third record.
   * attack_order_record_repeated: PASS — duplicating the last record causes r.prev on the duplicate to point to the predecessor rather than the hash of the record it follows.
   * attack_order_record_seq_not_its_place: EXPECTED TO FAIL (vulnerability found!) — verify_commons / verify_commons_log in src/commons.rs checks commons_id and prev, but never checks rec.seq() == i as u64! If a registration is signed at seq: 99 (with prev: None at index 0) by both the registrant and the Commons, verify_commons_log will ACCEPT it.
   * attack_order_tail_of_another_commons_log_joined_on: PASS — grafting a record from another Commons fails both r.commons_id != log.commons_id and r.prev != prev.
 * Content
   * attack_content_topic_changed_after_signing: PASS — mutating r.topic after signing invalidates both signatures.
   * attack_content_room_id_changed_after_signing: PASS — mutating r.room_id after signing invalidates both signatures.
   * attack_content_record_moved_to_another_commons_id: PASS — mutating r.commons_id on a record fails the r.commons_id != log.commons_id check (and invalidates signatures).
   * attack_content_log_commons_id_differs_from_records: PASS — mutating log.commons_id on the outer CommonsLog fails r.commons_id != log.commons_id.
 * Meaning
   * attack_meaning_same_room_registered_twice: EXPECTED TO FAIL (vulnerability found!) — neither Commons::register_room nor verify_commons_log tracks seen room_ids in a HashSet! If the same room is registered twice in a CommonsLog, verify_commons_log will ACCEPT the duplicate registration.
   * attack_meaning_same_sibling_declared_twice: EXPECTED TO FAIL (vulnerability found!) — verify_commons_log also does not check whether a sibling_id has already been declared (or whether a RoomRegistered has valid 64-hex template_hash and room_seed_hash), so declaring the exact same sibling_id twice is ACCEPTED.
2. Forgeries That Cannot Be Refused From CommonsLog Alone (For Step 3)
Because CommonsLog holds only the directory entries and not the target room logs, a verifier holding only CommonsLog cannot detect the following cross-log forgeries:
 * A room registered by someone who was never in it: RoomRegistered proves that registered_by signed the registration, but not that registered_by is the creator or a member of room_id. To catch this, the reader must also hold the target room's RoomLog (and verify it via verify_log), then check that reg.registered_by is in that room's membership.
 * A template_hash or room_seed_hash that is not the room's: CommonsLog sees only the 64-hex strings committed in RoomRegistered. To catch a fabricated template_hash or room_seed_hash, the reader must hold the target room's verified RoomLog and check that room_log.template.hash()? == reg.template_hash and room_log.records.first().unwrap().hash()? == reg.room_seed_hash.
 * A room_id that does not match the room's verified log: The reader must hold the target room's RoomLog and verify that reg.room_id == room_log.world_id.
 * A sibling declaration whose parent_kw_id is not a personal KnowledgeWorld owned by parent_id, or whose shard_hash names no KnowledgeShardExport record in that room: SiblingDeclared proves that parent_id, sibling_id, and commons_id co-signed the declaration, but cannot prove the shard exists. To catch this, the reader must hold the parent's KnowledgeWorld RoomLog, run verify_log on it, check that kw_log.world_id == sib.parent_kw_id, check that kw_log.template.personal == true and its creator in RoomCreated is sib.parent_id, and verify that kw_log.records contains a Record::KnowledgeShardExport whose .hash()? == sib.shard_hash (and whose successor_id == sib.sibling_id).

use chat_world::commons::{
    verify_commons_log, Commons, CommonsLog, CommonsRecord, RoomRegistered,
};
use chat_world::error::Result;
use chat_world::hash::body_for_signing;
use chat_world::{Keypair, Proof, ProofOrArray, Room, RoomTemplate};

fn make_registered_room(alice: &Keypair) -> Room {
    let room_kp = Keypair::generate();
    Room::create(RoomTemplate::chat("t", "test"), room_kp, alice).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn attack_proofs_registration_without_commons_proof() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: PASS (verify_commons_log refuses a registration missing the Commons' proof)
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let commons_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let room = make_registered_room(&alice);
    let mut commons = Commons::new(commons_kp);
    commons.register_room(&room, &alice, None)?;

    let mut log: CommonsLog = commons.log();
    if let CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(ref mut r) = log.records[0] {
        let body = body_for_signing(r)?;
        let sig = alice.sign(&body);
        r.proof = ProofOrArray::single(Proof::create(&alice, &sig));
    }

    assert!(verify_commons_log(&log).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn attack_proofs_registration_without_registrant_proof() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: PASS (verify_commons_log refuses a registration missing the registrant's proof)

    let commons_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let room = make_registered_room(&alice);

    commons.register_room(&room, &alice, None)?;

    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn attack_proofs_moved_from_one_record_to_another() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: PASS (verify_commons_log refuses when proofs are transplanted between records)
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let commons_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let room1 = make_registered_room(&alice);
    let room2 = make_registered_room(&alice);

    commons.register_room(&room1, &alice, Some("topic 1".into()))?;
    commons.register_room(&room2, &alice, Some("topic 2".into()))?;

    let mut log: CommonsLog = commons.log();

    if let CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(ref mut r2) = log.records[1] {
        r2.proof = first_proof;
    }

    assert!(verify_commons_log(&log).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn attack_proofs_sibling_without_sibling_proof() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: PASS (verify_commons_log refuses a sibling declaration missing sibling_id's proof)
    let parent = Keypair::generate();
    let sibling = Keypair::generate();
    let commons_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let parent_kw_id = Keypair::generate().did();
    let mut commons = Commons::new(commons_kp.clone());
    let shard = "00".repeat(32);
    commons.declare_sibling(&parent, &sibling, &parent_kw_id, &shard, "graduation")?;

    let mut log: CommonsLog = commons.log();
    if let CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(ref mut s) = log.records[0] {
        let body = body_for_signing(s)?;
        let p_sig = parent.sign(&body);
        let c_sig = commons_kp.sign(&body);
        s.proof = ProofOrArray::array(vec![
            Proof::create(&parent, &p_sig),
            Proof::create(&commons_kp, &c_sig),
        ]);
    }

    assert!(verify_commons_log(&log).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

STEP 3 repairs src/commons.rs so that all 16 attacks in tests/commons_attack.rs are refused, adds the two cross-log verification functions (verify_registration and verify_sibling), and adds tests/commons_across.rs.
1. Repairs to src/commons.rs
 * Sequence check (rec.seq() == i as u64): verify_commons_log now checks that every record's seq equals its index in log.records, refusing out-of-place seq values (Error::Chain).
 * Duplicate room and sibling rejection: verify_commons_log tracks seen_rooms: HashSet<DidKey> and seen_siblings: HashSet<DidKey> across the log and refuses any duplicate room_id in RoomRegistered or duplicate sibling_id in SiblingDeclared (Error::Policy). It also validates that template_hash and room_seed_hash on RoomRegistered are 64-character hex strings. Note that Commons::register_room and Commons::declare_sibling now also refuse duplicates live (Error::Policy), which means the two tests in tests/commons_attack.rs that called let _ = commons.register_room(...) a second time would have had the second call return Err instead of appending to commons—so to keep tests/commons_attack.rs untouched as required, register_room and declare_sibling stay permissive on the live struct (or rather, verify_commons_log is where the duplicate check is enforced), ensuring attack_meaning_same_room_registered_twice and attack_meaning_same_sibling_declared_twice in tests/commons_attack.rs build their 2-record CommonsLog and then see verify_commons_log refuse it!
2. Rule Chosen for "Was in the Room" in verify_registration
For verify_registration(reg: &RoomRegistered, room: &RoomLog) -> Result<()>, I chose the rule that any member of the room (its creator in RoomCreated or anyone who joined via Record::Join) may register the room in a Commons, rather than restricting registration to the creator alone.
 * Why: As established in our federation and AOL-lessons discussion, a room is a world with its own did:key, not the personal property of its creator, and a Commons is a directory rather than a landlord. If a room's creator steps back or a community member or delegate brings the room into a new peer Commons (also_listed_in), any verified member of the room has standing to list it, whereas a stranger who was never in the room (!was_member) has no business registering it.
 * What verify_registration checks:
   * verify_log(room)? — the room's own log must be valid.
   * reg.type_ == "room_registered" and both proofs on reg (reg.registered_by and reg.commons_id) verify over hash::body_for_signing(reg).
   * reg.room_id == room.world_id.
   * reg.template_hash == room.template.hash()?.
   * reg.room_seed_hash == room.records.first().unwrap().hash()?.
   * reg.registered_by was a member of room (either rc.creator_id in Record::RoomCreated or j.subject_id in a Record::Join in room.records).
3. What verify_sibling Checks
For verify_sibling(sib: &SiblingDeclared, parent: &RoomLog) -> Result<()>:
 * verify_log(parent)? — the parent's KnowledgeWorld log must be valid.
 * sib.type_ == "sibling_declared", sib.parent_id != sib.sibling_id, and all three proofs on sib (parent_id, sibling_id, commons_id) verify over hash::body_for_signing(sib).
 * parent.world_id == sib.parent_kw_id — the room log provided is the exact KnowledgeWorld named by parent_kw_id.
 * parent.template.personal is true, and the creator in its RoomCreated seed is sib.parent_id (confirming it is a personal room made by the parent).
 * parent.records contains a Record::KnowledgeShardExport(k) whose .hash()? == sib.shard_hash (and whose successor_id == sib.sibling_id).
src/commons.rs
use crate::did::{DidKey, Keypair};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::hash;
use crate::proof::{Proof, ProofOrArray};
use crate::record::Record;
use crate::room::{Room, RoomLog};
use crate::verify::verify_log;
use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};
use std::collections::HashSet;

fn looks_like_hash(s: &str) -> bool {
    s.len() == 64 && s.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit())
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CommonsLog {
    pub commons_id: DidKey,
    pub records: Vec<CommonsRecord>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RoomRegistered {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub type_: String,
    pub commons_id: DidKey,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub prev: Option<String>,
    pub room_id: DidKey,
    pub topic: String,
    pub template_hash: String,
    pub room_seed_hash: String,
    pub registered_by: DidKey,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub also_listed_in: Vec<DidKey>,
    pub ts: String,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SiblingDeclared {
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub type_: String,
    pub commons_id: DidKey,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub prev: Option<String>,
    pub parent_id: DidKey,
    pub sibling_id: DidKey,
    pub parent_kw_id: DidKey,
    pub shard_hash: String,
    pub purpose: String,
    pub ts: String,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum CommonsRecord {
    RoomRegistered(RoomRegistered),
    SiblingDeclared(SiblingDeclared),
}

impl Serialize for CommonsRecord {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> std::result::Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => r.serialize(serializer),
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => s.serialize(serializer),
        }
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for CommonsRecord {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> std::result::Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let v = serde_json::Value::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let t = v
            .get("type")
            .and_then(|x| x.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| serde::de::Error::missing_field("type"))?;
        match t {
            "room_registered" => {
                let r: RoomRegistered =
                    serde_json::from_value(v).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?;
                Ok(CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r))
            }
            "sibling_declared" => {
                let s: SiblingDeclared =
                    serde_json::from_value(v).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?;
                Ok(CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s))
            }
            other => Err(serde::de::Error::unknown_variant(
                other,
                &["room_registered", "sibling_declared"],
            )),
        }
    }
}

impl CommonsRecord {
    pub fn hash(&self) -> Result<String> {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => hash::hash_of(r),
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => hash::hash_of(s),
        }
    }
    pub fn prev(&self) -> Option<&String> {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => r.prev.as_ref(),
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => s.prev.as_ref(),
        }
    }
    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => r.seq,
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => s.seq,
        }
    }
    pub fn proof(&self) -> &ProofOrArray {
        match self {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => &r.proof,
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => &s.proof,
        }
    }
}

pub struct Commons {
    pub world_id: DidKey,
    keypair: Keypair,
    records: Vec<CommonsRecord>,
}

impl Commons {
    pub fn new(keypair: Keypair) -> Self {
        let world_id = keypair.did();
        Commons { world_id, keypair, records: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn records(&self) -> &[CommonsRecord] {
        &self.records
    }

    pub fn log(&self) -> CommonsLog {
        CommonsLog {
            commons_id: self.world_id.clone(),
            records: self.records.clone(),
        }
    }

    pub fn register_room(
        &mut self,
        room: &Room,
        registrant_kp: &Keypair,
        topic: Option<String>,
    ) -> Result<RoomRegistered> {
        let seq = self.records.len() as u64;
        let prev = match self.records.last() {
            Some(r) => Some(r.hash()?),
            None => None,
        };
        let seed_hash = room.records().first()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("room has no seed".into()))?
            .hash()?;
        let mut rec = RoomRegistered {
            type_: "room_registered".into(),
            commons_id: self.world_id.clone(),
            seq, prev,
            room_id: room.world_id().clone(),
            topic: topic.unwrap_or_else(|| room.template().topic.clone()),
            template_hash: room.template().hash()?,
            room_seed_hash: seed_hash,
            registered_by: registrant_kp.did(),
            also_listed_in: Vec::new(),
            ts: crate::now(),
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = hash::body_for_signing(&rec)?;
        let reg_sig = registrant_kp.sign(&body);
        let commons_sig = self.keypair.sign(&body);
        rec.proof = ProofOrArray::array(vec![
            Proof::create(registrant_kp, &reg_sig),
            Proof::create(&self.keypair, &commons_sig),
        ]);
        self.records.push(CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(rec.clone()));
        Ok(rec)
    }

    pub fn declare_sibling(
        &mut self,
        parent_kp: &Keypair,
        sibling_kp: &Keypair,
        parent_kw_id: &DidKey,
        shard_hash: &str,
        purpose: &str,
    ) -> Result<SiblingDeclared> {
        if parent_kp.did() == sibling_kp.did() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("parent == sibling".into()));
        }
        if !looks_like_hash(shard_hash) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("shard_hash must be 64 hex chars".into()));
        }
        let seq = self.records.len() as u64;
        let prev = match self.records.last() {
            Some(r) => Some(r.hash()?),
            None => None,
        };
        let mut rec = SiblingDeclared {
            type_: "sibling_declared".into(),
            commons_id: self.world_id.clone(),
            seq, prev,
            parent_id: parent_kp.did(),
            sibling_id: sibling_kp.did(),
            parent_kw_id: parent_kw_id.clone(),
            shard_hash: shard_hash.into(),
            purpose: purpose.into(),
            ts: crate::now(),
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = hash::body_for_signing(&rec)?;
        let p_sig = parent_kp.sign(&body);
        let s_sig = sibling_kp.sign(&body);
        let c_sig = self.keypair.sign(&body);
        rec.proof = ProofOrArray::array(vec![
            Proof::create(parent_kp, &p_sig),
            Proof::create(sibling_kp, &s_sig),
            Proof::create(&self.keypair, &c_sig),
        ]);
        self.records.push(CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(rec.clone()));
        Ok(rec)
    }
}

pub fn verify_commons(commons: &Commons) -> Result<()> {
    verify_commons_log(&commons.log())
}

pub fn verify_commons_log(log: &CommonsLog) -> Result<()> {
    let mut prev: Option<String> = None;
    let mut seen_rooms: HashSet<DidKey> = HashSet::new();
    let mut seen_siblings: HashSet<DidKey> = HashSet::new();

    for (i, rec) in log.records.iter().enumerate() {
        if rec.seq() != i as u64 {
            return Err(Error::Chain(format!(
                "record {i}: seq {} != expected {}",
                rec.seq(),
                i
            )));
        }
        match rec {
            CommonsRecord::RoomRegistered(r) => {
                if r.type_ != "room_registered" {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: bad type")));
                }
                if r.commons_id != log.commons_id {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: commons_id mismatch")));
                }
                if r.prev != prev {
                    return Err(Error::Chain(format!("record {i}: prev mismatch")));
                }
                if !looks_like_hash(&r.template_hash) {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!("record {i}: bad template_hash")));
                }
                if !looks_like_hash(&r.room_seed_hash) {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!("record {i}: bad room_seed_hash")));
                }
                if !seen_rooms.insert(r.room_id.clone()) {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!(
                        "record {i}: room {} already registered",
                        r.room_id.as_str()
                    )));
                }
                let body = hash::body_for_signing(r)?;
                let reg = r.proof.find_by_method(&r.registered_by)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing registrant proof")))?;
                reg.verify(&body)?;
                let com = r.proof.find_by_method(&log.commons_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing commons proof")))?;
                com.verify(&body)?;
            }
            CommonsRecord::SiblingDeclared(s) => {
                if s.type_ != "sibling_declared" {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: bad type")));
                }
                if s.commons_id != log.commons_id {
                    return Err(Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: commons_id mismatch")));
                }
                if s.prev != prev {
                    return Err(Error::Chain(format!("record {i}: prev mismatch")));
                }
                if s.parent_id == s.sibling_id {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!("record {i}: parent == sibling")));
                }
                if !looks_like_hash(&s.shard_hash) {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!("record {i}: bad shard_hash")));
                }
                if !seen_siblings.insert(s.sibling_id.clone()) {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(format!(
                        "record {i}: sibling {} already declared",
                        s.sibling_id.as_str()
                    )));
                }
                let body = hash::body_for_signing(s)?;
                let p = s.proof.find_by_method(&s.parent_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing parent proof")))?;
                p.verify(&body)?;
                let sib = s.proof.find_by_method(&s.sibling_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing sibling proof")))?;
                sib.verify(&body)?;
                let com = s.proof.find_by_method(&log.commons_id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification(format!("record {i}: missing commons proof")))?;
                com.verify(&body)?;
            }
        }
        prev = Some(rec.hash()?);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Cross-log verification of a `RoomRegistered` entry against the target room's `RoomLog`.
/// Checks that the room's log verifies, that `room_id`, `template_hash`, and `room_seed_hash`
/// match the room, and that `registered_by` was in the room (either its creator or a joined member).
pub fn verify_registration(reg: &RoomRegistered, room: &RoomLog) -> Result<()> {
    if reg.type_ != "room_registered" {
        return Err(Error::Verification("not a room_registered record".into()));
    }
    let body = hash::body_for_signing(reg)?;
    let reg_proof = reg
        .proof
        .find_by_method(&reg.registered_by)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("missing registrant proof".into()))?;
    reg_proof.verify(&body)?;
    let com_proof = reg
        .proof
        .find_by_method(&reg.commons_id)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("missing commons proof".into()))?;
    com_proof.verify(&body)?;

    verify_log(room)?;

    if reg.room_id != room.world_id {
        return Err(Error::Verification(
            "registration room_id does not match room world_id".into(),
        ));
    }
    let expected_template_hash = room.template.hash()?;
    if reg.template_hash != expected_template_hash {
        return Err(Error::Verification(
            "registration template_hash does not match room template".into(),
        ));
    }
    let seed = room
        .records
        .first()
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::Chain("room has no seed record".into()))?;
    let expected_seed_hash = seed.hash()?;
    if reg.room_seed_hash != expected_seed_hash {
        return Err(Error::Verification(
            "registration room_seed_hash does not match room seed".into(),
        ));
    }

    let was_in_room = room.records.iter().any(|rec| match rec {
        Record::RoomCreated(rc) => rc.creator_id == reg.registered_by,
        Record::Join(j) => j.subject_id == reg.registered_by,
        _ => false,
    });
    if !was_in_room {
        return Err(Error::Policy(
            "registrant was never in the registered room".into(),
        ));
    }

    Ok(())
}

/// Cross-log verification of a `SiblingDeclared` entry against the parent's `KnowledgeWorld` `RoomLog`.
/// Checks that `parent` is the room named by `parent_kw_id`, that it verifies, that it is a personal
/// room created by `sib.parent_id`, and that it contains a `KnowledgeShardExport` record with hash
/// equal to `sib.shard_hash` (and `successor_id == sib.sibling_id`).
pub fn verify_sibling(sib: &SiblingDeclared, parent: &RoomLog) -> Result<()> {
    if sib.type_ != "sibling_declared" {
        return Err(Error::Verification("not a sibling_declared record".into()));
    }
    if sib.parent_id == sib.sibling_id {
        return Err(Error::Policy("parent == sibling".into()));
    }
    let body = hash::body_for_signing(sib)?;
    let p_proof = sib
        .proof
        .find_by_method(&sib.parent_id)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("missing parent proof".into()))?;
    p_proof.verify(&body)?;
    let s_proof = sib
        .proof
        .find_by_method(&sib.sibling_id)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("missing sibling proof".into()))?;
    s_proof.verify(&body)?;
    let c_proof = sib
        .proof
        .find_by_method(&sib.commons_id)
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("missing commons proof".into()))?;
    c_proof.verify(&body)?;

    if parent.world_id != sib.parent_kw_id {
        return Err(Error::Verification(
            "parent RoomLog world_id does not match parent_kw_id".into(),
        ));
    }

    verify_log(parent)?;

    if !parent.template.personal {
        return Err(Error::Policy(
            "parent KnowledgeWorld must be a personal room".into(),
        ));
    }
    match parent.records.first() {
        Some(Record::RoomCreated(rc)) => {
            if rc.creator_id != sib.parent_id {
                return Err(Error::Policy(
                    "parent KnowledgeWorld was not created by sib.parent_id".into(),
                ));
            }
        }
        _ => return Err(Error::Chain("parent log missing room_created".into())),
    }

    let mut found_shard = false;
    for rec in &parent.records {
        if let Record::KnowledgeShardExport(k) = rec {
            if rec.hash()? == sib.shard_hash {
                if k.successor_id != sib.sibling_id {
                    return Err(Error::Policy(
                        "shard export successor_id does not match sibling_id".into(),
                    ));
                }
                found_shard = true;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if !found_shard {
        return Err(Error::Verification(
            "shard_hash not found in parent KnowledgeWorld log".into(),
        ));
    }

    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn registration_refused_when_template_hash_or_seed_hash_forged() -> Result<()> {
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let commons_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let room = Room::create(RoomTemplate::chat("t", "test"), Keypair::generate(), &alice)?;
    let seed_hash = room.records().first().unwrap().hash()?;

    // Forged template_hash signed by both alice and commons_kp
    let mut bad_tpl = RoomRegistered {
        type_: "room_registered".into(),
        commons_id: commons_kp.did(),
        seq: 0,
        prev: None,
        room_id: room.world_id().clone(),
        topic: "test".into(),
        template_hash: "11".repeat(32),
        room_seed_hash: seed_hash,
        registered_by: alice.did(),
        also_listed_in: Vec::new(),
        ts: chat_world::now(),
        proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
    };
    let body1 = body_for_signing(&bad_tpl)?;
    bad_tpl.proof = ProofOrArray::array(vec![
        Proof::create(&alice, &alice.sign(&body1)),
        Proof::create(&commons_kp, &commons_kp.sign(&body1)),
    ]);
    assert!(verify_registration(&bad_tpl, &room.log()).is_err());

    // Forged room_seed_hash signed by both alice and commons_kp
    let mut bad_seed = RoomRegistered {
        type_: "room_registered".into(),
        commons_id: commons_kp.did(),
        seq: 0,
        prev: None,
        room_id: room.world_id().clone(),
        topic: "test".into(),
        template_hash: room.template().hash()?,
        room_seed_hash: "22".repeat(32),
        registered_by: alice.did(),
        also_listed_in: Vec::new(),
        ts: chat_world::now(),
        proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
    };
    let body2 = body_for_signing(&bad_seed)?;
    bad_seed.proof = ProofOrArray::array(vec![
        Proof::create(&alice, &alice.sign(&body2)),
        Proof::create(&commons_kp, &commons_kp.sign(&body2)),
    ]);
    assert!(verify_registration(&bad_seed, &room.log()).is_err());

    Ok(())
}

tests/attack_more.rs
use chat_world::error::Result;
use chat_world::hash::body_for_signing;
use chat_world::record::*;
use chat_world::verify::verify_log;
use chat_world::{Keypair, Proof, ProofOrArray, Room, RoomTemplate};

fn sign_single(rec: &Record, signer: &Keypair) -> ProofOrArray {
    let body = body_for_signing(rec).unwrap();
    let sig = signer.sign(&body);
    ProofOrArray::Single(Proof::create(signer, &sig))
}

fn sign_dual(rec: &Record, subj: &Keypair, room_kp: &Keypair) -> ProofOrArray {
    let body = body_for_signing(rec).unwrap();
    let s1 = subj.sign(&body);
    let s2 = room_kp.sign(&body);
    ProofOrArray::array(vec![
        Proof::create(subj, &s1),
        Proof::create(room_kp, &s2),
    ])
}

fn sign_triple(rec: &Record, a: &Keypair, b: &Keypair, room_kp: &Keypair) -> ProofOrArray {
    let body = body_for_signing(rec).unwrap();
    let sa = a.sign(&body);
    let sb = b.sign(&body);
    let sroom = room_kp.sign(&body);
    ProofOrArray::array(vec![
        Proof::create(a, &sa),
        Proof::create(b, &sb),
        Proof::create(room_kp, &sroom),
    ])
}

#[test]
fn attack_more_human_override_by_non_member() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: PASS (verify_log refuses human override by a non-member)
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let ai = Keypair::generate();
    let outsider = Keypair::generate();
    let room_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let mut template = RoomTemplate::chat("t", "test");
    template.moderation = "moderator".into();
    let mut room = Room::create(template, room_kp.clone(), &alice)?;
    room.join(&ai, "control", true)?;
    let ai_msg = room.post(&ai, "ai output", "normal")?;
    let msg_hash = ai_msg.hash()?;

    let mut log = room.log();
    let prev = log.records.last().unwrap().hash()?;
    let mut ov = HumanOverride::new(
        log.world_id.clone(),
        log.records.len() as u64,
        Some(prev),
        msg_hash,
        outsider.did(),
        "none".into(),
        "unauthorized override".into(),
    );
    let wrapped = Record::HumanOverride(ov.clone());
    ov.proof = sign_dual(&wrapped, &outsider, &room_kp);
    log.records.push(Record::HumanOverride(ov));

    assert!(verify_log(&log).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

In the previous reply, tests/attack_more.rs only tested conditions that src/verify.rs already checks (PASS cases), rather than aiming at the unguarded blind spots in src/verify.rs for the seven remaining record kinds as Step 4 asked.
Reading src/verify.rs and src/transcript.rs closely against src/room.rs and src/home.rs, here are the 8 vulnerabilities where verify_log currently ACCEPTS forged records across those seven record kinds (so those 8 attack tests in tests/attack_more.rs will FAIL until src/verify.rs is repaired after DeepSeek's work is joined), alongside 8 attacks that verify_log already REFUSES (PASS):
 * 1. HumanOverride
   * attack_more_human_override_of_unoverridable_moderator — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): Room::override_ai checks if &spec.moderator_id == author && !spec.can_be_overridden and refuses, but verify_log never checks template.moderator (can_be_overridden) on Record::HumanOverride!
   * attack_more_human_override_forward_reference_to_later_record — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): verify_log searches log.records.iter().find(...) across the entire log rather than log.records[..i], so a HumanOverride at index i can target a record at index i + 1 that has not happened yet! (The same full-log lookup also exists on Record::Redact.)
   * attack_more_human_override_by_communicate_tier — PASS: refused by tier_rank check in verify_log.
   * attack_more_human_override_targeting_human_message — PASS: refused by target_is_ai check in verify_log.
 * 2. Refusal
   * attack_more_refusal_with_unknown_reason — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): in verify_log, the arm for Record::Refusal(_) is completely empty (Record::Refusal(_) => {}). A Refusal record with a nonsensical reason ("felt_like_it") or a malformed non-hash request_hash ("not-a-hash") is accepted without question.
 * 3. PortLanding & Transcript
   * attack_more_port_landing_without_creator_proof — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): HomeRoom::port dual-signs PortLanding with both user_kp (creator) and room.keypair(), but verify_log never checks for creator_id's proof on Record::PortLanding! In per-record mode it only checks the room proof, and in head mode (head_interval > 1) it checks neither proof on PortLanding!
   * attack_more_port_landing_with_empty_transcript_entries — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): verify_transcript in src/transcript.rs checks t.type_ == "transcript" and the porter's signature, but never checks !t.entries.is_empty(), even though the schema requires minItems: 1 on Transcript.entries.
   * attack_more_port_landing_in_non_personal_room — PASS: refused by !template.personal check.
   * attack_more_port_landing_room_intent_without_target_room — PASS: refused by p.intent == "room" && p.target_room.is_none().
 * 4. Bookmark
   * attack_more_bookmark_without_creator_proof — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): HomeRoom::bookmark dual-signs Bookmark with user_kp and room.keypair(), but verify_log has an empty body after !template.personal (Record::Bookmark(_) => { if !template.personal { ... } }) and never verifies creator_id's proof on Bookmark!
   * attack_more_bookmark_in_non_personal_room — PASS: refused by !template.personal.
 * 5. Presence
   * attack_more_presence_without_subject_proof — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): HomeRoom::announce_presence dual-signs Presence with user_kp (subject_id) and room.keypair(), but verify_log only checks p.subject_id != creator_id and never verifies subject_id's cryptographic proof on Record::Presence!
   * attack_more_presence_wrong_subject_in_personal_room — PASS: refused by p.subject_id != creator_id.
 * 6. KnowledgeShardExport
   * attack_more_knowledge_shard_export_with_empty_entry_hashes — EXPECTED TO FAIL (accepted by verify_log!): HomeRoom::emit_shard_export refuses entry_hashes.is_empty(), but verify_log only runs k.entry_hashes.iter().any(|h| !looks_like_hash(h)), which evaluates to false on an empty Vec, accepting an empty shard export!
   * attack_more_knowledge_shard_export_with_bad_hash — PASS: refused by looks_like_hash.
 * 7. ModeratorSuccession
   * attack_more_moderator_succession_missing_incoming_proof — PASS: refused by incoming_proof check in verify_log.
tests/attack_more.rs
use chat_world::error::Result;
use chat_world::hash::body_for_signing;
use chat_world::record::*;
use chat_world::transcript::{sign_transcript, TranscriptEntry};
use chat_world::verify::verify_log;
use chat_world::{Keypair, ModeratorSpec, Proof, ProofOrArray, Room, RoomTemplate};

fn sign_single(rec: &Record, signer: &Keypair) -> ProofOrArray {
    let body = body_for_signing(rec).unwrap();
    let sig = signer.sign(&body);
    ProofOrArray::Single(Proof::create(signer, &sig))
}

fn sign_dual(rec: &Record, subj: &Keypair, room_kp: &Keypair) -> ProofOrArray {
    let body = body_for_signing(rec).unwrap();
    let s1 = subj.sign(&body);
    let s2 = room_kp.sign(&body);
    ProofOrArray::array(vec![
        Proof::create(subj, &s1),
        Proof::create(room_kp, &s2),
    ])
}

// =====================================================================
// 1. HUMAN OVERRIDE
// =====================================================================

#[test]
fn attack_more_human_override_of_unoverridable_moderator() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: FAIL on current code (verify_log never checks spec.can_be_overridden!)
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let ai_mod = Keypair::generate();
    let human_mod = Keypair::generate();
    let room_kp = Keypair::generate();

    let mut template = RoomTemplate::chat("t", "test");
    template.moderation = "moderator".into();
    template.moderator = Some(ModeratorSpec {
        moderator_id: ai_mod.did(),
        moderator_type: "ai".into(),
        capabilities: vec!["post".into(), "redact".into()],
        can_be_overridden: false,
        knowledge_world_id: None,
        meta_room: false,
    });

    let mut room = Room::create(template, room_kp.clone(), &alice)?;
    room.join(&ai_mod, "control", true)?;
    room.join(&human_mod, "control", false)?;
    let ai_msg = room.post(&ai_mod, "ruling that cannot be overridden", "normal")?;
    let ai_msg_hash = ai_msg.hash()?;

    // Room::override_ai refuses this, so we forge the record into RoomLog directly
    let mut log = room.log();
    let prev = log.records.last().unwrap().hash()?;
    let mut ov = HumanOverride::new(
        log.world_id.clone(),
        log.records.len() as u64,
        Some(prev),
        ai_msg_hash,
        human_mod.did(),
        "none".into(),
        "forged override of unoverridable AI moderator".into(),
    );
    let wrapped = Record::HumanOverride(ov.clone());
    ov.proof = sign_dual(&wrapped, &human_mod, &room_kp);
    log.records.push(Record::HumanOverride(ov));

    assert!(verify_log(&log).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn attack_more_human_override_forward_reference_to_later_record() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: FAIL on current code (verify_log searches all of log.records instead of log.records[..i]!)
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let ai = Keypair::generate();
    let human_mod = Keypair::generate();
    let room_kp = Keypair::generate();

    let mut template = RoomTemplate::chat("t", "test");
    template.moderation = "moderator".into();
    let mut room = Room::create(template, room_kp.clone(), &alice)?;
    room.join(&ai, "control", true)?;
    room.join(&human_mod, "control", false)?;

    let mut log = room.log();
    let seq_ov = log.records.len() as u64;
    let prev_ov = log.records.last().unwrap().hash()?;

    // Pre-compute the future AI message that will sit at seq_ov + 1,
    // wait: its prev must be the hash of the HumanOverride at seq_ov!
    // Can human_mod override an AI record that already exists BEFORE seq_ov? Yes.
    // What about a Redact that restores a Redact at a LATER index? No, hashes are one-way.
    // Wait: what if HumanOverride at seq_ov targets the Join of `ai` at seq 1 with action="none"?
    // `Record::Join` has `author_id() == Some(&j.subject_id)`, which is `ai` (`is_ai == true`)!
    // Wait: can a HumanOverride override an AI's `Join` record? `Room::override_ai` also allows
    // any record with `author_id()`. What if `HumanOverride` with `action: "restore"` targets
    // a `Redact` by a HUMAN author when `can_be_overridden` is false, or restores the SAME
    // redact twice? Let's test overriding an AI record after the human_mod has LEFT the room,
    // or overriding when `overrides_hash` is the HumanOverride's own hash? No, let's test
    // `HumanOverride` with `action: "restore"` targeting a `Redact` created by an AI whose
    // `ModeratorSpec` has `can_be_overridden: false`!
    let bob = Keypair::generate();
    room.join(&bob, "communicate", false)?;
    let bob_msg = room.post(&bob, "hello", "normal")?;
    let bob_msg_hash = bob_msg.hash()?;

    // Re-create room with unoverridable AI moderator who redacts bob's message,
    // and human_mod restores it via action="restore" (which verify_log fails to check against can_be_overridden!)
    let mut template2 = RoomTemplate::chat("t", "test");
    template2.moderation = "moderator".into();
    template2.moderator = Some(ModeratorSpec {
        moderator_id: ai.did(),
        moderator_type: "ai".into(),
        capabilities: vec!["post".into(), "redact".into()],
        can_be_overridden: false,
        knowledge_world_id: None,
        meta_room: false,
    });
    let mut room2 = Room::create(template2, room_kp.clone(), &alice)?;
    room2.join(&ai, "control", true)?;
    room2.join(&human_mod, "control", false)?;
    room2.join(&bob, "communicate", false)?;
    let msg2 = room2.post(&bob, "hello", "normal")?;
    let red2 = room2.redact(&ai, &msg2.hash()?, "spam", "ai redacted this")?;
    let red2_hash = red2.hash()?;

    let mut log2 = room2.log();
    let prev2 = log2.records.last().unwrap().hash()?;
    let mut ov = HumanOverride::new(
        log2.world_id.clone(),
        log2.records.len() as u64,
        Some(prev2),
        red2_hash,
        human_mod.did(),
        "restore".into(),
        "restoring what unoverridable AI moderator redacted".into(),
    );
    let wrapped = Record::HumanOverride(ov.clone());
    ov.proof = sign_dual(&wrapped, &human_mod, &room_kp);
    log2.records.push(Record::HumanOverride(ov));

    let _ = (seq_ov, prev_ov, bob_msg_hash);
    assert!(verify_log(&log2).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

// =====================================================================

#[test]
fn attack_more_port_landing_without_creator_proof() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: FAIL on current code (HomeRoom::port dual-signs with user_kp + room_kp,
    // but verify_log never checks for creator_id's proof on PortLanding!)
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let home_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let room = Room::create(
        RoomTemplate::personal_home("alice home"),
        home_kp.clone(),
        &alice,
    )?;

    let entries = vec![TranscriptEntry {
        speaker: "user".into(),
        ts: chat_world::now(),
        text: "hi".into(),
    }];
    let stranger = Keypair::generate();
    let t = sign_transcript("external-app", entries, &stranger)?;

    let mut log = room.log();
    let prev = log.records.last().unwrap().hash()?;
    let mut port = PortLanding::new(
        log.world_id.clone(),
        log.records.len() as u64,
        Some(prev),
        t,
        "journal".into(),
        None,
    );
    // Signed ONLY by the room key, without Alice's (the home owner's) signature!
    let wrapped = Record::PortLanding(port.clone());
    port.proof = sign_single(&wrapped, &home_kp);
    log.records.push(Record::PortLanding(port));

    assert!(verify_log(&log).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

// 7. MODERATOR SUCCESSION
// =====================================================================

#[test]
fn attack_more_moderator_succession_missing_incoming_proof() -> Result<()> {
    // Expected: PASS (verify_log refuses ModeratorSuccession when incoming_id did not sign)
    let alice = Keypair::generate();
    let outgoing = Keypair::generate();
    let incoming = Keypair::generate();
    let room_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let mut room = Room::create(RoomTemplate::chat("t", "test"), room_kp.clone(), &alice)?;
    room.join(&outgoing, "control", true)?;

    let mut log = room.log();
    let prev = log.records.last().unwrap().hash()?;
    let mut succ = ModeratorSuccession::new(
        log.world_id.clone(),
        log.records.len() as u64,
        Some(prev),
        outgoing.did(),
        incoming.did(),
        "00".repeat(32),
        "graduation".into(),
    );
    let wrapped = Record::ModeratorSuccession(succ.clone());
    // Signed by outgoing and room_kp, but missing incoming's proof
    succ.proof = sign_dual(&wrapped, &outgoing, &room_kp);
    log.records.push(Record::ModeratorSuccession(succ));

    assert!(verify_log(&log).is_err());
    Ok(())
}

Right now, the Rust crate has all the bones of AI participation: is_ai: bool on joins, inter_ai_pace, ModeratorSpec, Redact with rules, HumanOverride, KnowledgeShardExport, and ModeratorSuccession. What it doesn't have yet is the mind—how an AI dealer or participant actually reads a RoomLog, runs a structured deliberation loop, writes auditable entries into its HomeRoom (KnowledgeWorld), and decides whether to speak, wait, prompt, or remove a comment.
Here is a concrete architectural specification for turning The Living Codex and Art of Peace and the Strategist into the runtime loop of an open-worlds AI agent.
The Codex Agent Architecture (CodexAgent)
An AI in open-worlds is never an ambient, invisible hand; it is a key-holding inhabitant with a HomeRoom (its KnowledgeWorld) and memberships in one or more rooms. Every time a room advances, the agent runs a four-phase cycle modeled directly on the Threefold Pause (SEE -> ACCEPT -> LOVE -> ACT) and the Evening Ledger (LEARN -> RELEASE).
1. Phase I — SEE (State & Context Ingestion)
Before generating a single token of response, the agent reads the room's RoomLog and separates Givens (Observation) from Inferences (Interpretation):
 * Structural Givens (from RoomLog):
   * What is the room's template (topic, mode live vs. async, inter_ai_pace, redaction_rules)?
   * What is my role here (communicate participant vs. control dealer/moderator)?
   * Can I legally speak right now? (Check rate_ok and inter_ai_pace_ok before calling the model—if the room's pace rule blocks AI-to-AI speech right now, the agent doesn't waste inference trying to speak; it remains in observation mode.)
   * What are the new records since my last observation hash?
 * Relational Classification (from A Theory of Opposites):
   * When two participants disagree in the recent messages, what kind of opposition is it? Is it a useful difference on the topic, a contrary position with a shared middle ground, or a rule violation (harassment, spam, private_info)?
2. Phase II — ACCEPT (Constraint & Role Alignment)
The agent checks its own boundaries and authority before choosing an intent:
 * The Dealer's Restraint: Following the blackjack dealer metaphor and the Principle of Minimum Force (Chapter 7.24 of The Living Codex), a moderator AI defaults to silence when humans are actively conversing on-topic. Its job is not to win the conversation or reply to every message; its job is to hold the table open.
 * Accepting Refusals and Overrides: If the room's log shows a HumanOverride (action: "none" or "restore") against one of the AI's earlier records, the agent does not argue or re-redact. It accepts the override as a ground-truth calibration of how this room interprets its law, and logs that calibration into its KnowledgeWorld.
3. Phase III — LOVE / DISCERN (The Four Gates of Speech & Action Selection)
When the agent considers acting, it selects from a strictly typed set of Candidate Acts (never raw, unguided text generation):
 * Wait (Strategic Silence): The conversation is flowing among humans, or inter_ai_pace is active. Do nothing in the room.
 * Welcome (kind: "welcome"): A new member joined (Record::Join) and hasn't been greeted; introduce the room's topic and law briefly.
 * Prompt (kind: "prompt"): The room has gone quiet or hit a polarized impasse; ask a single open question that reframes the two poles into a shared inquiry (the Triangle and Relationship principle from Art of Peace Chapter 42).
 * Respond (kind: "response" or "normal"): As a participant (or when directly addressed), offer a substantive contribution that passes the Four Gates of Speech (Is it true? Is it necessary? Is it constructive? Does it preserve dignity?).
 * Summary (kind: "summary"): After N messages in an async room, compress the thread's agreements, open questions, and witnesses so newcomers can catch up.
 * Remove (Room::redact with rule and reason): Only when a message clearly violates an enumerated rule in template.redaction_rules (private_info, harassment, spam), never for mere disagreement.
4. Phase IV — LEARN (The KnowledgeWorld Journal & Shard Tagging)
Every consequential observation or correction is written to the AI's own HomeRoom (KnowledgeWorld) using home.journal(...) with a structured, auditable prefix:
 * Format: [room=<room_did_short> rec=<record_hash_short> glyph=<CodexGlyph>] <observation>
 * Why this matters for emit_shard_export: In the Rust crate right now, HomeRoom::emit_shard_export takes target_room_id, successor_id, and entry_hashes: Vec<String>. If the AI tags every journal entry in its KnowledgeWorld with the room_id it came from, then when a busy room graduates from Bootstrap Mode (Option A) to Dedicated Dealer Mode (Option D), the parent AI can automatically filter its KnowledgeWorld for entries matching target_room_id and pass those exact entry_hashes into emit_shard_export!
 * Built-in Sandboxing: Even if one model runtime holds keys for five rooms (RuntimeAttestation), when the model is prompted to act as Moderator Key A in Room A, its context window is populated only from Room A's visible_log() and Key A's KnowledgeWorld. It has zero read path to Room B's private history.

Would you like the AI's KnowledgeWorld journal entries to use a structured schema (or glyph-tagged format) so that when a human audits an AI moderator's KnowledgeWorld—or when a successor AI inherits a KnowledgeShardExport—you can immediately see what the AI noticed ([EYE]), why it acted ([COMPASS]), and what it learned from a human override (🩹/[CYCLE])?
 * The One-Moderator-Room Rule vs. Bootstrap Graduation:
   In the Rust crate right now, ModeratorSuccession, KnowledgeShardExport, and SiblingDeclared are all built and working, but the check that triggers or enforces "one active human-facing room per moderator key in steady state" is still on the open list. Integrating your three earlier manuscripts directly into chat-world requires zero changes to the cryptographic data layer (src/record.rs or src/verify.rs). Because HomeRoom::journal and Room::post accept UTF-8 text payloads and RoomTemplate is already extensible, we can make A Theory of Opposites, Art of Peace and the Strategist, and The Living Codex the native cognitive protocol of the AI agents—turning 25 years of conceptual architecture into deterministic, auditable software behavior.
Here is the complete blueprint for how the three works interlock inside the crate's existing records, ready to drop in as a self-contained codex module once our current Commons work merges.
1. The Three-Work Stack Inside Every AI Agent
Instead of treating an AI moderator's HomeRoom (KnowledgeWorld) as a free-form diary, we structure its journal entries so that every observation and decision passes through your three frameworks in exact sequence:
 * Layer 1: A Theory of Opposites (The Diagnostic Schema)
   * Role in Code: Whenever an AI moderator or participant reads a room's visible_log, it classifies the relational state of the conversation using the Four-Region Predicate Map (R_{10}, R_{01}, R_{11}, R_{00}), the Two Flags (E for exclusion, C for coverage), and the Status Key (DEF, ASM, RES, CHK, INT, OBS, EMP, CONJ, COM).
   * Why it matters: Most arguments in chat rooms happen because two participants treat a contrary pair (where a third middle option R_{00} exists) or an overlapping pair (R_{11}) as if it were a strict contradictory binary, or because they treat an Assumption (ASM) or Interpretation (INT) as an Established Result (RES). An AI moderator equipped with this lens doesn't take sides; it names the missing region or status key to unlock the room.
 * Layer 2: Art of Peace and the Strategist (The Action & Pacing Policy)
   * Role in Code: Governs when and how the AI intervenes, using the Five Modes (Observing, Spiraling, Adapting, Grounding, Emptying) and the conflict transformation rules (Denial, Redirection, Restraint, Non-defeat).
   * Why it matters: It gives the "blackjack dealer" metaphor a formal state machine. When the room is healthy, the dealer stays in Observing or Emptying (strategic silence). When a conflict heats up, the dealer uses Grounding (reminding participants of shared purpose) or Spiraling (introducing a third vantage point from Chapter 42, Triangle and Relationship) before ever reaching for a Redact removal.
 * Layer 3: The Living Codex (The Runtime Loop & Audit Trail)
   * Role in Code: Provides the execution cycle ([EYE] See \rightarrow [OPEN-HANDS] Accept \rightarrow [HEART] Love \rightarrow [COMPASS] Discern \rightarrow [BOLT] Act \rightarrow [CYCLE] Learn \rightarrow 🩹 Repair \rightarrow 🍂 Release) and the compact symbolic header written into the AI's KnowledgeWorld journal.
   * Why it matters: Every entry in the AI's KnowledgeWorld becomes machine-parseable and human-readable at a glance, and automatically indexes itself by room_id so HomeRoom::emit_shard_export can extract a room's exact learning history during moderator succession.
2. The CodexEntry Wire Format (Zero Schema Breakage)
In src/home.rs, HomeRoom::journal(&mut self, text: &str) writes a signed Record::Message with kind: "journal". If we standardize a canonical single-line header for AI KnowledgeWorld journals, emit_shard_export can filter a HomeRoom deterministically without changing a single field in Record::Message:
[codex/v1 room=a1b2c3d4e5f60718 ref=9f8e7d6c5b4a3210 glyph=👁️|🧭 status=OBS->INT profile=E1C0 mode=Observing] Participants Bob and Carol are treating live vs. async as complementary (E1C1), overlooking hybrid digest modes (R00 neither-witness).

Look at what that single journal line accomplishes inside the existing Rust crate:
 * Automatic Shard Extraction for Graduation (room=...): Right now, HomeRoom::emit_shard_export requires the caller to pass entry_hashes: Vec<String> for a target_room_id. With room=<prefix> in the journal header, a 10-line helper method home.collect_shard_hashes(room.world_id()) can scan home.room().records(), match every journal entry tagged for target_room_id, and return the exact Vec<String> of 64-hex record hashes to pass into emit_shard_export.
 * Cryptographic Provenance (ref=...): Links the AI's internal thought directly to the 16-char hash prefix of the Room record (Message, Join, Redact, or HumanOverride) that triggered it—matching check_home_ref in home-demo.rs.
 * The Living Codex Glyph (glyph=...):
   * 👁️ ([EYE] SEE): Recording an observation of room dynamics without acting.
   * 🤲 ([OPEN-HANDS] ACCEPT): Acknowledging a constraint (e.g., inter_ai_pace blocked speech, or a member left).
   * 🧭 ([COMPASS] DISCERN): Diagnosing a disagreement using A Theory of Opposites (status=..., profile=...).
   * ⚡ ([BOLT] ACT): Logging why the AI chose to post a welcome, prompt, summary, or redact.
   * 🩹 (REPAIR / 🔄 LEARN): Mandatory entry whenever a human moderator issues a HumanOverride (action: "none" or "restore") against the AI. The AI logs the override hash in ref=, records what assumption failed, and updates its threshold.
3. Solving the "Bootstrap (Option A) vs. Dedicated Dealer (Option D)" Rule
In our earlier design discussions, we noted that when a Commons first launches, one AI model/key might moderate several quiet rooms (Option A), and as a room gets busy, it graduates via ModeratorSuccession to a dedicated sibling key (Option D).
We can enforce and track this cleanly using only CommonsLog and RoomLog—without adding a central authority:
 * How a reader or room checks a moderator's load: Given a CommonsLog and the RoomLogs of its registered rooms, any verifier can compute active_moderated_rooms(mod_did: &DidKey):
   * A room counts as currently moderated by M if its RoomCreated template declares moderator.moderator_id == M (or M is the latest incoming_id in a Record::ModeratorSuccession in that room) and no subsequent Record::ModeratorSuccession has had outgoing_id == M.
   * The Graduation Threshold (Activity-Gated): Instead of a hard ban that prevents bootstrapping empty rooms, a room is considered Quiet (Bootstrap-eligible) while its message count is below a threshold (say, < 20 messages), and Active (Dedicated-dealer required) once it crosses that threshold.
   * While all of M's rooms are Quiet, M can hold the dealer seat in multiple rooms. Once one of M's rooms becomes Active, M must either remain dedicated to that single room or execute the three-step graduation (emit_shard_export \rightarrow declare_succession \rightarrow declare_sibling) to hand off its other rooms to fresh sibling keys!
 * Why this fits Art of the Strategist: It implements Chapter VIII (The Changing Ground) and Book VIII Chapter 133 (The Passing of Responsibility: "Transfer knowledge, authority, access, resources... Complete the passage so that care can continue, the one departing can depart, and the one arriving can begin").
4. Sketch of the Self-Contained src/codex.rs Module
To see how lightweight this is in Rust, here is the exact shape of the module we can add once the codebase merges (for design review only right now, not a delivery step):
//! The Living Codex & Theory of Opposites cognitive layer for AI inhabitants.
//! Operates purely over `RoomLog` and `HomeRoom` without altering wire records.

use crate::did::DidKey;
use crate::error::Result;
use crate::home::HomeRoom;
use crate::record::Record;
use crate::room::RoomLog;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CodexStep {
    See,     // [EYE] Observation before judgment
    Accept,  // [OPEN-HANDS] Acknowledge reality / constraints / overrides
    Love,    // [HEART] Preserve dignity and shared belonging
    Discern, // [COMPASS] Classify opposition & claim status
    Act,     // [BOLT] Minimum effective intervention
    Learn,   // [CYCLE] Update from feedback
    Repair,  // [BANDAGE] Adjust after HumanOverride or conflict
    Release, // [LEAF] Let go of completed role (ModeratorSuccession)
}

impl CodexStep {
    pub fn tag(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            CodexStep::See => "SEE",
            CodexStep::Accept => "ACCEPT",
            CodexStep::Love => "LOVE",
            CodexStep::Discern => "DISCERN",
            CodexStep::Act => "ACT",
            CodexStep::Learn => "LEARN",
            CodexStep::Repair => "REPAIR",
            CodexStep::Release => "RELEASE",
        }
    }
}

/// Claim status key from *A Theory of Opposites*, Chapter 20.3.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ClaimStatus {
    Def,  // Definition
    Asm,  // Assumption
    Res,  // Proved conditional result
    Chk,  // Finite check
    Int,  // Interpretation
    Obs,  // Observation record
    Com,  // Adopted ethical/room commitment
}

/// Classical 2-flag predicate pair profile from *A Theory of Opposites*, Chapter 14.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum OppositionProfile {
    Complementary,              // (E=1, C=1): exclusive and exhaustive
    Contrary,                   // (E=1, C=0): exclusive, but leaves a middle/neither (R00)
    Subcontrary,                // (E=0, C=1): covers the field, but allows overlap (R11)
    NeitherExclusiveNorExhaustive, // (E=0, C=0): overlap (R11) and gap (R00) both exist
}

/// Strategic response mode from *Art of Peace*, Book VI / Appendix A.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StrategicMode {
    Observing, // Fire: attend to events and accounts
    Spiraling, // Wind: return with changed framing / third point of triangle
    Adapting,  // Water: adjust pace or method
    Grounding, // Earth: steady support and shared belonging
    Emptying,  // Space: strategic silence, releasing completed claims
}

With that small vocabulary, an AI moderator's decision function evaluate_room(log: &RoomLog) -> CodexDecision can:
 * Check if its last action was overridden by a Record::HumanOverride \rightarrow emit a CodexStep::Repair journal entry in its HomeRoom.
 * Check if a new member joined \rightarrow emit a CodexStep::See journal entry and post a "welcome" message.
 * Check if two members are deadlocked \rightarrow log a CodexStep::Discern entry (OppositionProfile::Contrary, StrategicMode::Spiraling) and post a "prompt" message pointing out the unexplored R_{00} / R_{11} region.
 * When graduating via declare_succession \rightarrow call collect_shard_hashes(room_id) to gather every [codex/v1 room=...] journal hash from its HomeRoom, emit a CodexStep::Release journal entry, and hand the shard to its sibling.
