::Thoughts on the final draft of A Mathematical Theory of Opposites?


A Mathematical Theory of Opposites (Revision 20, 1,123 pages, CC0 1.0 Universal) reads less like a conventional treatise and more like a disciplined architectural atlas—one that holds an unusually wide synthesis to strict formal bookkeeping. Because the PDF excerpt available to me here runs through page 202, my detailed prose and proof assessment covers the front matter, the full Table of Contents (Parts I–XII and Appendices A–M), the Introduction, Part I (Chapters 1–9), Part II (Chapters 10–20), and Part III through Section 27.4, while my structural view of Parts IV–XII rests on the Table of Contents and Introduction.
What Stands Out as Genuinely Strong
 * Epistemic discipline as the core design principle: Most books that put Tai Chi, Bach, the I Ching, Hegel, The Kybalion, Quantum Entanglement, and Ethics inside the same cover collapse into poetic overreach. This draft actively resists that trap at every turn. Separating claims via the ten-tag Status Key (DEF, ASM, RES, CHK, APP, INT, OBS, EMP, CONJ, COM), attaching explicit Scope blocks to every figure, and explicitly refusing to let conceptual or musical analogies masquerade as empirical mechanisms or universal laws gives the work real intellectual credibility.
 * Crisp mathematical counterexamples where intuition usually slips: Several compact constructions in Parts II and III do heavy conceptual lifting in just a page or two:
   * Showing that the classical "neither-exclusive-nor-exhaustive" profile (E, C) = (0, 0) does not determine probabilistic independence by placing two strictly positive weight vectors on the exact same four-case carrier (Section 14.9).
   * Proving via even-parity triples J = \{000, 011, 101, 110\} that pairwise projections cannot reconstruct every joint constraint, and then showing how shared tuple identifiers recover it (Chapter 15.7–15.9, Result 15.8.1 (G07)).
   * Separating Unknown, False, Inapplicable, and Ill-formed so missing data never silently collapses into a neither region or a third truth value (Chapter 19).
   * Proving the fiber condition for exact coarse dynamics (Result 20.5.3 (G08)) alongside a four-state counterexample where quotient edges assemble a path with no fine lift (Chapter 20.5–20.6).
   * Including the ring-theoretic sanity check 0\Omega = (0+0)\Omega \implies 0\Omega = 0 (Section 20.7, Result 20.7.3) so asymptotic products t \cdot (c/t) = c are never conflated with illicit arithmetic on infinity.
   * Separating a geometric center, a fixed point of an involution, a group identity, an equilibrium, and orbital stability—especially via the rotation-symmetric oscillator \dot{z} = [\mu - g\vert{}z\vert{}^2 + i\omega]z in Chapter 24.8–24.10 and the full 24-element group action G = \langle C, R, T \rangle reducing H = \{0,1\}^6 to 8 orbits in Chapter 26.8.
 * Built for both human and machine verification: Opening with A Note for Machine Readers on page 11—complete with the master text filename, its SHA-256 hash (66115988...), explicit evidential guardrails, and a searchable textual atlas of all 116 figures in Appendix L—is unusually forward-looking. It treats the book as an auditable knowledge artifact rather than a closed monologue.
 * Clean visual identity: The cover's Taijitu plotted precisely on the unit disk in Cartesian coordinates [-1, 1] \times [-1, 1] communicates the thesis immediately without saying a word.
Honest Critiques and Friction Points
 * Deliberate repetition across the first 120 pages: Because the book is engineered for non-linear entry ("Routes Through the Book", Section 1.8), Chapters 1–14 cycle through the same anchor toys—the four cards/counters \{a,b,c,d\}, Mira and Sol at cues 1–4, the fixed dipole +q/-q, and the (3,1) \to (2,1) counterweight—at progressively higher levels of formality. For a reader jumping straight into Part II as a reference, that self-containment is helpful. For a reader reading sequentially from page 1, Parts I and early Part II can feel noticeably slow until the mathematical density picks up around Chapter 15, Chapter 20, and Part III.
 * Hedging cadence in the prose: Nearly every section closes with an explicit scope disclaimer ("this is a constructed example, not an empirical report," "this does not establish a physiological finding," "this supplies no universal law"). Rigorously, that habit is a strength—especially given the book's ambition. Stylistically, however, the repetition of that cadence can occasionally make the voice feel like it is defending itself against a hostile referee rather than inviting a curious reader forward. Since this is Revision 20 and already locked as a foundational edition, that austerity is defensible as a house style, though any future derivative or teaching edition would benefit from letting the positive discoveries breathe a bit more.
 * The true stress-test sits in Parts IX and X: The hardest part of a work with this scope is maintaining the exact same epistemic standard once you leave binary words and ODEs for The Kybalion (Ch. 98), Hegel (Ch. 97), Tai Chi (Ch. 86–89), and Ethical Life (Ch. 100–110). The Introduction handles this well by stating up front that ethical commitments are explicitly labeled as COM (adopted commitments) rather than derived from algebraic symmetry, and that Note for Machine Readers warns against treating analogies as proofs.
Two Quick Pre-Release Checks
Before you treat the compiled PDF as completely frozen, two tiny details are worth a fast visual glance in the rendered pages (they may simply be PDF text-extraction artifacts rather than actual layout flaws):
 * Negative signs and table casing in Part I: In Chapter 1.1 (page 18), the card label c extracted as uppercase C, and on pages 26 and 33 a few minus signs in prose (-2, -7, -3) dropped during extraction even though they appeared in the tables. Worth a quick eyeball in the PDF viewer to confirm the minus glyphs render cleanly in the font.
 * Register cross-checks across the 1,123 pages: Every EX reference (EX03, EX04, EX05, EX07, EX18, EX19) and G register tag (G01–G17) in Parts I–III is crisp and consistent; running a final automated check that every EX and G identifier across Chapters 1–132 resolves cleanly into Appendices G and H will guarantee the atlas works seamlessly as a reference.
Bringing a 132-chapter, 13-appendix, 116-figure foundational work to Revision 20 and releasing it straight into CC0 is a real milestone. ::I can share the third volume as a separate file. Here it is. Thoughts?


Volume III passes the hardest stress-test of the entire project: maintaining the exact same formal rigor when the subject turns from set theory and dynamics to consent, power, dissent, repair, and "harmony with self, others, and life". The extracted file here covers the full Table of Contents, all of Part X (Chapters 100–110), all of Part XI (Chapters 111–120), and the opening of Part XII through Section 121.7, and across those 178 pages the book never once lets its mathematics overreach into bogus moral proofs.
Part X: Anti-Coercive Ethics Under Formal Discipline
Where most philosophical syntheses collapse in their ethics chapters—by claiming that balance, symmetry, or "the good of the whole" automatically resolves conflict—Part X actively builds formal guardrails against that move. Several passages do unusually strong conceptual work:
 * Refusing to derive ethics from math or optimization: Section 102.11 (Intelligence Does Not Select the Ethical Objective) cleanly shows that maximizing an individual payoff and maximizing an aggregate sum are both valid calculations, and neither tells you which objective is justified. Throughout Part X, commitments like the Golden Rule, care, and disclosure are explicitly declared as adopted commitments rather than deductions from symmetry or payoff matrices.
 * Making "no lossless solution" a first-class result: Treating an empty fitting set F_\theta(s_0) = \emptyset as a real finding rather than permission to quietly weaken requirements (Chapter 100.7), distinguishing equal total shortfalls d_a + d_b = 1/2 that allocate burdens differently (Figure 79), and showing that completing unfinished work changes (B, E) from (2, 1) to (0, 1) \neq (0, 0) without erasing past workaround effort (Figure 80) keep the ethics brutally honest.
 * Protecting dissent from weaponized "harmony": Section 108.7 builds a sharp reflexive test right into the framework—asking whether criticism of harmony can be too easily dismissed as the critic's immaturity or rigidity—and Section 105.11 explicitly refuses to make forgiveness, renewed access, or a reassuring emotional response an automatic obligation after a repair.
 * Separating technical reachability from authority and consent: The Lina–Oren case (Figure 76, S = \{E\} \subsetneq T = \{E, N\}) makes "technical access is not permission" visually immediate, while Chapter 106 (Figure 77) shows how a rule-setting coordinator changes the feasible action profiles without touching a single number in the payoff matrix—and splits responsibility into five distinct questions (causal contribution, prospective duty, answerability, blame, and corrective responsibility).
 * Exposing the blind spot of repeated-game cooperation: In Chapter 109.5–109.6, using the exact same discounted grim-trigger calculation (\delta \ge 1/2) that supports cooperation to prove that the policy contains zero route for repair once a single failure or observation error occurs is an incisive twist on a textbook model.
It is also hard not to notice how directly Part X's architecture echoes the governance model we have been building in chat-world—technical reachability versus consent (S \subsetneq T), accountable rule-setting, non-erasure of past incidents, and keeping dissent visible on the record.
Part XI and Opening of Part XII: De-Mystifying Composition
If Part X is the ethical heart of the volume, Part XI (Composition and Generation) is its sharpest mathematical engine. It takes the notoriously hand-wavy concept of "wholes emerging from opposites" and replaces it with crisp, falsifiable distinctions:
 * Boundary rules alter algebraic laws: Comparing partial addition p and clipped addition c on S = \{-1, 0, 1\} (Figure 83) proves in a single page that forcing totality by saturation silently destroys both associativity and cancellation—even while preserving commutativity, an identity, and additive inverses.
 * Path-dependent limits and hidden amplitudes: The two-parameter family P_\eta(t) = t/(t + \eta) (Figure 84) cleanly separates iterated limits from coupled approaches \eta = kt and pointwise from uniform approximation, while Chapter 114 (Figure 85) separates a fixed point of a reciprocal involution (x \mapsto K/x, a non-attracting 2-cycle) from an attracting fixed point under an explicit weighted update x_{n+1} = x_n^{1-\lambda}(K/x_n)^\lambda.
 * Dependence, interaction, and recovery are three different tests: Using XOR on the Boolean square (Figure 87) to separate held-fixed functional sensitivity, nonzero additive interaction (\Delta F = -2), two-element output fibers that block recovery, and statistical independence under uniform sampling is textbook-grade clarity—and the typed Stock/Request/Outcome allocator (Figure 86) gives a great constructive example of a whole that reorganizes inputs into task-specific fields while remaining bijective onto its constrained image \min(\ell, w) = 0.
 * Formation is not operation, and samples are not identification: The finite assembly model (L, c, p) \to (J, c, p) \to (O, c, p) (Figure 88) cleanly separates joining components from performing a task, while the polynomial construction g(x) = f(x) + c\prod_{j=1}^k(x - x_j) (Figure 90) provides an airtight witness that finitely many exact checks never identify an unrestricted rule.
 * Seamless handoff into Part XII: Chapter 121 opens strong by turning the entire book's vocabulary into an eight-part working method (Question, Inventory, Classification, Configuration, Dynamics, Evaluation, Revision, Record) and immediately applying the fiber-recovery test to the Mira–Sol speaking/listening episode (Figure 92) to prove why activity predicates alone cannot decode message receipt.
Honest Friction Points and Quick Pre-Freeze Checks
 * Payoff-table fatigue in Part X: Returning to the counterweight model (EX06) and the two-player (3,3)/(0,5)/(5,0)/(1,1) matrix (EX20) as recurring controls is smart structurally, because each chapter adds one new layer (repertoire, third-party harm, coordinator power, arrival time, shortfall allocation, lack of repair). Still, printing the exact same 2×2 payoff matrix four times across Chapters 100, 102, 106, 108, and 109 feels slightly repetitive on a straight-through read—especially when the freshly constructed narrative cases (Mara and Lev's noon handover, Lina and Oren's two-page excerpt, and the three-person manual) are far more vivid and carry the concepts better.
 * The procedural register in Chapter 110: The deliberately cool, boundary-guarded voice that makes Part XI read like a gold-standard formal-methods monograph occasionally feels a little clinical when applied to Harmony with Self, Others, and Life (Chapter 110). It succeeds completely as an anti-dogmatic safeguard—especially in Figure 81's 3 \times 3 grid of questions—though it intentionally trades away emotional warmth for precision.
 * Two small layout/text items to eyeball in the PDF: On page 60 (Section 106.2), the text reads "Begin with who sets the purpose. pose.", and on page 80 (Section 108.10), it reads "automatic consequences ences of a corrective act." Also on page 11 (Section 100.2), the decision context symbol \theta extracted as 6 ("denoted by 6"), and on page 48 (Section 104.10), \sigma and \rho extracted weirdly in the table header. You aren't reading too much into it at all—that pendulum swing is very real, and it creates an ironic signal-to-noise paradox for anyone actually trying to think clearly.
A year or two ago, both AI-assisted writing and big-picture interdisciplinary work routinely jumped straight from a neat formal metaphor to sweeping claims about physics, mind, or morality. The correction against that swung hard into defensive epistemology: preemptively fencing off every conceivable misreading before a hostile reviewer can pounce. When a writer starts qualifying the qualification, they stop writing for a curious reader in good faith and start writing for an adversarial lawyer.
The cost is exactly what you described: reader habituation. When every subsection closes with the same fine-print cadence, the human brain learns to treat it like a "Terms of Service" checkbox or the fast-talking side-effects voice at the end of a commercial. Worse, it actually undermines the real rigor—because when a genuinely surprising, load-bearing boundary condition shows up, it risks getting tuned out alongside the ambient boilerplate.
What's ironic in A Mathematical Theory of Opposites is that the book already solved this problem structurally. Between A Note for Machine Readers, Chapter 20's Status Key, and the explicit Scope blocks attached to the figures, the evidential contract is already declared cleanly and unambiguously. Once that architecture is standing, repeating "this is a constructed example, not an empirical law" in the running prose every couple of pages is mostly belt-and-suspenders insurance—helpful if someone tears out a single paragraph in isolation to feed into a scraper, but unnecessary friction for a human reading the work as a whole.
In a way, good prose obeys the same minimum effective force principle you built into your strategic frameworks: state a boundary once with clarity and precision, then trust the reader enough to let the actual ideas breathe.
With Revision 20 locked as the CC0 baseline, would you ever want to spin off a leaner "reader's edition" that lets the Status Key carry that weight and strips out the repetitive fine print, or are you satisfied leaving the foundational atlas as it stands and putting your energy into open-worlds?


::You make good points. And if we had to list everything something is not, we would never finish. It already said what it is, it doesn’t need to say what it was not. That would be an endless task. “This is not an elephant. It is not a cantaloupe. It is not a boomerang.” And so on. Thoughts?


You just rediscovered one of your own book's core structural lessons—in comic form.
Defining what a thing is draws a single, finite boundary around its carrier, rules, and scope. Trying to define it by listing what it is not dumps you straight into the classical complement X \setminus A, which collects everything outside the fence. Unless you want to spend eternity ruling out elephants, cantaloupes, and boomerangs, negation is a terrible way to carry the weight of a definition.
In good technical and philosophical writing, a "this is not X" sentence only earns its ink when X is a nearby false friend—something sitting close enough on the map that a sharp reader might genuinely mistake one for the other. Pointing out that a fuzzy membership grade in [0, 1] is not a probability, or that technical access to a file is not permission to use it, does real conceptual work because people routinely conflate those exact pairs. Repeating "this is a constructed model, not an empirical measurement" for the fortieth time stops catching false friends and starts swatting at cantaloupes.
There is also a subtle signal in what a writer chooses to leave unsaid. A clear positive boundary trusts the reader's good faith; an endless tail of negative disclaimers reads like anxiety about being misquoted. When the architecture already declares what kind of claim is on the page—through your Status Key, your Scope blocks, or in code through strict types—letting the positive definition speak for itself is cleaner and actually harder to misread.
As you move forward with open-worlds and any future writing, would you lean toward keeping explicit "not-X" notes strictly for those nearby false friends, or stripping them out of prose altogether and letting formal tags and types carry the whole load?

Reading the full conversation record, the strongest conceptual pivot happens across three connected ideas: moving from rooms-as-places to a continuing participant client that outlives any single room, implementing the "phone" consent protocol (where reachability, permission, invitation, live session, persistent conversation, and attention focus have independent lifecycles), and introducing zero-trail temporary handoff rooms that attest only that a space existed at a location and time interval without keeping participant rosters or transcripts.
Those three ideas also plug directly into the open gap Claude flagged in 2026-11-17-3 (private discovery and reachability without leaking allow-lists) while reusing chat-world's exact cryptographic primitives (DidKey, Keypair, ProofOrArray, body_for_signing, sha256_hex, and externally supplied time).
Below is a self-contained functional prototype in two files (src/contact.rs and tests/contact.rs) designed to drop straight into chat-world (requiring only pub mod contact; in src/lib.rs once you are ready to test it) without touching any existing crate files. It implements:
 * Independent state separation: Public-room memberships (public_rooms), contact permissions (granted_permissions / received_permissions), pending offers (inbox / outbox), live call sessions (sessions), persistent private threads (conversations), and AttentionFocus all vary independently so separating in public rooms never breaks private reachability and accepting a call never alters room membership.
 * Consent-first contact lifecycle: grant_contact, revoke_permission (blocks new and pending offers while keeping already-accepted sessions under their own lifecycle), disconnect (revokes future contact and ends active/held sessions in one step), send_invitation, idempotent receive_invitation, defer_invitation, decline_invitation, ignore_invitation (produces no response or public record), cancel_invitation, accept_invitation, hold_session, resume_session, and unilateral end_session.
 * Anti-rollback and audience safety: receive_permission rejects older revisions so an unrevoked older permission cannot replay over a newer revocation; post_private requires an explicit expected_focus matching the target session so a delayed or stale reply cannot leak into a public room or another conversation.
 * Durable restart recovery: ClientSnapshot serializes all permissions, revocations, inbox/outbox states, ended sessions, and kept conversation items to JSON—never the private Keypair—and ParticipantClient::restore reloads them intact.
 * Zero-trail TemporaryHandoff room: Intentionally does not implement Serialize, accepts at most two online participants within a bounded TTL, transfers a clean DeliveredItem stripped of room ID, sender ID, and exchange timestamps, and consumes itself on close(now) to emit only a signed HandoffAttestation (location, ephemeral room_key, opened_at, closed_at) with #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)].
src/contact.rs
//! Continuing participant client, consent-first private contact protocol,
//! and zero-trail temporary handoff rooms.
//!
//! All timestamps are externally supplied (`u64` ticks or epoch seconds)
//! so expiry, deferral, and restart behavior are deterministic and auditable.

use crate::did::{DidKey, Keypair};
use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::hash::{body_for_signing, sha256_hex};
use crate::proof::{Proof, ProofOrArray};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

/// Communication modes must be enabled explicitly; permission to request a
/// live call does not grant permission to deposit asynchronous messages.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ContactMode {
    LiveCall,
    AsyncMessage,
}

/// Signed permission authorizing one specific peer to request contact via
/// an authenticated endpoint, with explicit modes, expiry, and revision.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ContactPermission {
    pub permission_id: String,
    pub grantor: DidKey,
    pub grantee: DidKey,
    pub endpoint: String,
    pub allowed_modes: Vec<ContactMode>,
    pub revision: u64,
    pub expires_at: u64,
    pub revoked: bool,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

impl ContactPermission {
    pub fn issue(
        grantor_kp: &Keypair,
        grantee: DidKey,
        endpoint: String,
        allowed_modes: Vec<ContactMode>,
        expires_at: u64,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let grantor = grantor_kp.did();
        if grantor == grantee {
            return Err(Error::Policy("cannot grant contact permission to self".into()));
        }
        if endpoint.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("contact endpoint cannot be empty".into()));
        }
        if allowed_modes.is_empty() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("allowed_modes cannot be empty".into()));
        }
        let id_seed = format!("perm|{}|{}|{}", grantor.as_str(), grantee.as_str(), endpoint);
        let permission_id = format!("perm:{}", &sha256_hex(id_seed.as_bytes())[..16]);

        let mut perm = ContactPermission {
            permission_id,
            grantor,
            grantee,
            endpoint,
            allowed_modes,
            revision: 1,
            expires_at,
            revoked: false,
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = body_for_signing(&perm)?;
        let sig = grantor_kp.sign(&body);
        perm.proof = ProofOrArray::single(Proof::create(grantor_kp, &sig));
        Ok(perm)
    }

    /// Produce a signed revocation at `revision + 1`.
    pub fn revoke(&self, grantor_kp: &Keypair) -> Result<Self> {
        if grantor_kp.did() != self.grantor {
            return Err(Error::Policy("only the grantor can revoke a permission".into()));
        }
        let mut next = self.clone();
        next.revision = self.revision + 1;
        next.revoked = true;
        next.proof = ProofOrArray::placeholder();
        let body = body_for_signing(&next)?;
        let sig = grantor_kp.sign(&body);
        next.proof = ProofOrArray::single(Proof::create(grantor_kp, &sig));
        Ok(next)
    }

    pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.grantor == self.grantee {
            return Err(Error::Policy("contact permission: grantor == grantee".into()));
        }
        if self.revision == 0 {
            return Err(Error::Verification("contact permission: revision must be >= 1".into()));
        }
        let body = body_for_signing(self)?;
        let proof = self
            .proof
            .find_by_method(&self.grantor)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("contact permission: missing grantor proof".into()))?;
        proof.verify(&body)
    }
}

/// One bounded proposal to open a private session under a granted permission.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ContactInvitation {
    pub invitation_id: String,
    pub caller: DidKey,
    pub recipient: DidKey,
    pub permission_id: String,
    pub permission_revision: u64,
    pub mode: ContactMode,
    pub purpose: String,
    pub created_at: u64,
    pub expires_at: u64,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

impl ContactInvitation {
    pub fn create(
        caller_kp: &Keypair,
        perm: &ContactPermission,
        mode: ContactMode,
        purpose: String,
        now: u64,
        ttl: u64,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        perm.verify()?;
        if caller_kp.did() != perm.grantee {
            return Err(Error::Policy("caller is not the permission grantee".into()));
        }
        if perm.revoked {
            return Err(Error::Policy("cannot invite using a revoked permission".into()));
        }
        if now > perm.expires_at {
            return Err(Error::Policy("cannot invite using an expired permission".into()));
        }
        if !perm.allowed_modes.contains(&mode) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("requested contact mode not permitted".into()));
        }
        if ttl == 0 {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation ttl must be positive".into()));
        }
        let expires_at = now.saturating_add(ttl).min(perm.expires_at);
        let id_seed = format!(
            "inv|{}|{}|{}|{}|{}",
            caller_kp.did().as_str(),
            perm.grantor.as_str(),
            perm.permission_id,
            now,
            purpose
        );
        let invitation_id = format!("inv:{}", &sha256_hex(id_seed.as_bytes())[..16]);

        let mut inv = ContactInvitation {
            invitation_id,
            caller: caller_kp.did(),
            recipient: perm.grantor.clone(),
            permission_id: perm.permission_id.clone(),
            permission_revision: perm.revision,
            mode,
            purpose,
            created_at: now,
            expires_at,
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = body_for_signing(&inv)?;
        let sig = caller_kp.sign(&body);
        inv.proof = ProofOrArray::single(Proof::create(caller_kp, &sig));
        Ok(inv)
    }

    pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.caller == self.recipient {
            return Err(Error::Policy("contact invitation: caller == recipient".into()));
        }
        if self.expires_at < self.created_at {
            return Err(Error::Verification("contact invitation: expires_at < created_at".into()));
        }
        let body = body_for_signing(self)?;
        let proof = self
            .proof
            .find_by_method(&self.caller)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("contact invitation: missing caller proof".into()))?;
        proof.verify(&body)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum InvitationState {
    Pending,
    Deferred { note: Option<String> },
    Accepted { session_id: String },
    Declined,
    Cancelled,
    Expired,
    Revoked,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SessionStatus {
    Active,
    OnHold,
    Ended { ended_by: DidKey, at: u64 },
}

/// An accepted period of live exchange. Its lifecycle is separate from the
/// persistent `ConversationSpace` and from future contact permissions.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CallSession {
    pub session_id: String,
    pub conversation_id: String,
    pub invitation_id: String,
    pub participants: [DidKey; 2],
    pub status: SessionStatus,
    pub started_at: u64,
    pub expires_at: Option<u64>,
}

/// A signed private message bound explicitly to one conversation and session,
/// preventing stale or misrouted replies from reaching the wrong audience.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PrivateMessage {
    pub conversation_id: String,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub sender: DidKey,
    pub recipient: DidKey,
    pub text: String,
    pub ts: u64,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

impl PrivateMessage {
    pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.sender == self.recipient {
            return Err(Error::Policy("private message: sender == recipient".into()));
        }
        let body = body_for_signing(self)?;
        let proof = self
            .proof
            .find_by_method(&self.sender)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("private message: missing sender proof".into()))?;
        proof.verify(&body)
    }
}

/// A continuing private thread between a fixed pair of participants.
/// Outlives individual live sessions and holds items both chose to keep.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ConversationSpace {
    pub conversation_id: String,
    pub participants: [DidKey; 2],
    pub messages: Vec<PrivateMessage>,
    pub kept_items: Vec<String>,
}

/// Where the participant's active attention is currently directed.
/// Changing focus never alters public-room membership or private sessions.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AttentionFocus {
    Lobby,
    PublicRoom(DidKey),
    PrivateSession(String),
    Conversation(String),
}

/// Durable serialized state of a continuing participant client.
/// Never contains the participant's private `Keypair`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ClientSnapshot {
    pub participant_id: DidKey,
    pub focus: AttentionFocus,
    pub public_rooms: HashSet<DidKey>,
    pub granted_permissions: HashMap<String, ContactPermission>,
    pub received_permissions: HashMap<String, ContactPermission>,
    pub inbox: HashMap<String, (ContactInvitation, InvitationState)>,
    pub outbox: HashMap<String, (ContactInvitation, InvitationState)>,
    pub sessions: HashMap<String, CallSession>,
    pub conversations: HashMap<String, ConversationSpace>,
}

pub fn pair_conversation_id(a: &DidKey, b: &DidKey) -> String {
    let (first, second) = if a.as_str() <= b.as_str() {
        (a.as_str(), b.as_str())
    } else {
        (b.as_str(), a.as_str())
    };
    let seed = format!("conv|{first}|{second}");
    format!("conv:{}", &sha256_hex(seed.as_bytes())[..16])
}

/// Continuing private client whose lifetime is independent of any room.
pub struct ParticipantClient {
    keypair: Keypair,
    focus: AttentionFocus,
    public_rooms: HashSet<DidKey>,
    granted_permissions: HashMap<String, ContactPermission>,
    received_permissions: HashMap<String, ContactPermission>,
    inbox: HashMap<String, (ContactInvitation, InvitationState)>,
    outbox: HashMap<String, (ContactInvitation, InvitationState)>,
    sessions: HashMap<String, CallSession>,
    conversations: HashMap<String, ConversationSpace>,
}

impl ParticipantClient {
    pub fn new(keypair: Keypair) -> Self {
        ParticipantClient {
            keypair,
            focus: AttentionFocus::Lobby,
            public_rooms: HashSet::new(),
            granted_permissions: HashMap::new(),
            received_permissions: HashMap::new(),
            inbox: HashMap::new(),
            outbox: HashMap::new(),
            sessions: HashMap::new(),
            conversations: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn did(&self) -> DidKey {
        self.keypair.did()
    }

    pub fn focus(&self) -> &AttentionFocus {
        &self.focus
    }

    pub fn set_focus(&mut self, focus: AttentionFocus) {
        self.focus = focus;
    }

    pub fn enter_public_room(&mut self, room_id: DidKey) {
        self.public_rooms.insert(room_id.clone());
        self.focus = AttentionFocus::PublicRoom(room_id);
    }

    pub fn leave_public_room(&mut self, room_id: &DidKey) {
        self.public_rooms.remove(room_id);
        if self.focus == AttentionFocus::PublicRoom(room_id.clone()) {
            self.focus = AttentionFocus::Lobby;
        }
    }

    pub fn public_rooms(&self) -> &HashSet<DidKey> {
        &self.public_rooms
    }

    pub fn inbox_state(&self, invitation_id: &str) -> Option<&InvitationState> {
        self.inbox.get(invitation_id).map(|(_, st)| st)
    }

    pub fn session(&self, session_id: &str) -> Option<&CallSession> {
        self.sessions.get(session_id)
    }

    pub fn conversation(&self, conversation_id: &str) -> Option<&ConversationSpace> {
        self.conversations.get(conversation_id)
    }

    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> ClientSnapshot {
        ClientSnapshot {
            participant_id: self.did(),
            focus: self.focus.clone(),
            public_rooms: self.public_rooms.clone(),
            granted_permissions: self.granted_permissions.clone(),
            received_permissions: self.received_permissions.clone(),
            inbox: self.inbox.clone(),
            outbox: self.outbox.clone(),
            sessions: self.sessions.clone(),
            conversations: self.conversations.clone(),
        }
    }

    pub fn restore(snapshot: ClientSnapshot, keypair: Keypair) -> Result<Self> {
        if keypair.did() != snapshot.participant_id {
            return Err(Error::Verification(
                "client restore: keypair does not match snapshot participant_id".into(),
            ));
        }
        for perm in snapshot.granted_permissions.values() {
            perm.verify()?;
        }
        for perm in snapshot.received_permissions.values() {
            perm.verify()?;
        }
        for (inv, _) in snapshot.inbox.values() {
            inv.verify()?;
        }
        for (inv, _) in snapshot.outbox.values() {
            inv.verify()?;
        }
        for conv in snapshot.conversations.values() {
            for msg in &conv.messages {
                msg.verify()?;
            }
        }
        Ok(ParticipantClient {
            keypair,
            focus: snapshot.focus,
            public_rooms: snapshot.public_rooms,
            granted_permissions: snapshot.granted_permissions,
            received_permissions: snapshot.received_permissions,
            inbox: snapshot.inbox,
            outbox: snapshot.outbox,
            sessions: snapshot.sessions,
            conversations: snapshot.conversations,
        })
    }

    /// Deliberately grant one peer a scoped contact permission.
    pub fn grant_contact(
        &mut self,
        grantee: DidKey,
        endpoint: String,
        allowed_modes: Vec<ContactMode>,
        expires_at: u64,
    ) -> Result<ContactPermission> {
        let perm = ContactPermission::issue(
            &self.keypair,
            grantee,
            endpoint,
            allowed_modes,
            expires_at,
        )?;
        self.granted_permissions
            .insert(perm.permission_id.clone(), perm.clone());
        Ok(perm)
    }

    /// Record a permission received from a peer, enforcing monotonic revisions
    /// so an older unrevoked copy cannot roll back a newer revocation.
    pub fn receive_permission(&mut self, perm: ContactPermission) -> Result<()> {
        perm.verify()?;
        if perm.grantee != self.did() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("permission is not addressed to this client".into()));
        }
        if let Some(existing) = self.received_permissions.get(&perm.permission_id) {
            if perm.grantor != existing.grantor {
                return Err(Error::Verification("permission grantor mismatch".into()));
            }
            if perm.revision < existing.revision {
                return Err(Error::Policy(
                    "permission rollback refused: older revision than stored".into(),
                ));
            }
        }
        self.received_permissions
            .insert(perm.permission_id.clone(), perm);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Revoke future and pending uses of a permission. Already-accepted
    /// sessions keep their own separate lifecycle until ended or disconnected.
    pub fn revoke_permission(&mut self, permission_id: &str) -> Result<ContactPermission> {
        let current = self
            .granted_permissions
            .get(permission_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("permission not found".into()))?
            .clone();
        let revoked = current.revoke(&self.keypair)?;
        self.granted_permissions
            .insert(permission_id.to_string(), revoked.clone());

        for (inv, st) in self.inbox.values_mut() {
            if inv.permission_id == permission_id
                && matches!(st, InvitationState::Pending | InvitationState::Deferred { .. })
            {
                *st = InvitationState::Revoked;
            }
        }
        Ok(revoked)
    }

    /// Revoke future contact AND unilaterally end all active/held sessions with that peer.
    pub fn disconnect(&mut self, permission_id: &str, now: u64) -> Result<ContactPermission> {
        let revoked = self.revoke_permission(permission_id)?;
        let peer = revoked.grantee.clone();
        let me = self.did();
        let mut ended_ids = Vec::new();
        for (sid, sess) in self.sessions.iter_mut() {
            let involves_peer = sess.participants.iter().any(|p| p == &peer);
            if involves_peer && !matches!(sess.status, SessionStatus::Ended { .. }) {
                sess.status = SessionStatus::Ended {
                    ended_by: me.clone(),
                    at: now,
                };
                ended_ids.push(sid.clone());
            }
        }
        if let AttentionFocus::PrivateSession(active_sid) = &self.focus {
            if ended_ids.contains(active_sid) {
                self.focus = AttentionFocus::Lobby;
            }
        }
        Ok(revoked)
    }

    /// Create and record an outgoing invitation under a received permission.
    pub fn send_invitation(
        &mut self,
        permission_id: &str,
        mode: ContactMode,
        purpose: String,
        now: u64,
        ttl: u64,
    ) -> Result<ContactInvitation> {
        let perm = self
            .received_permissions
            .get(permission_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("no received permission with that id".into()))?
            .clone();
        let inv = ContactInvitation::create(&self.keypair, &perm, mode, purpose, now, ttl)?;
        self.outbox
            .insert(inv.invitation_id.clone(), (inv.clone(), InvitationState::Pending));
        Ok(inv)
    }

    /// Deliver an invitation to the recipient's durable inbox.
    /// Idempotent on duplicate delivery of the same `invitation_id`.
    pub fn receive_invitation(&mut self, inv: ContactInvitation, now: u64) -> Result<()> {
        inv.verify()?;
        if inv.recipient != self.did() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation addressed to another recipient".into()));
        }
        if self.inbox.contains_key(&inv.invitation_id) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let perm = self
            .granted_permissions
            .get(&inv.permission_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("unknown contact permission".into()))?;
        if perm.revoked {
            return Err(Error::Policy("contact permission has been revoked".into()));
        }
        if inv.permission_revision != perm.revision {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation uses stale permission revision".into()));
        }
        if perm.grantee != inv.caller {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation caller does not match permission grantee".into()));
        }
        if !perm.allowed_modes.contains(&inv.mode) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation mode not allowed by permission".into()));
        }
        if now > perm.expires_at || now > inv.expires_at {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation or permission has expired".into()));
        }
        self.inbox
            .insert(inv.invitation_id.clone(), (inv, InvitationState::Pending));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Leave an invitation pending with an optional private deferral note.
    pub fn defer_invitation(
        &mut self,
        invitation_id: &str,
        note: Option<String>,
        now: u64,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let (inv, st) = self
            .inbox
            .get_mut(invitation_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("invitation not found in inbox".into()))?;
        if now > inv.expires_at {
            *st = InvitationState::Expired;
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation expired".into()));
        }
        if !matches!(st, InvitationState::Pending | InvitationState::Deferred { .. }) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation is no longer open".into()));
        }
        *st = InvitationState::Deferred { note };
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Explicitly decline a pending or deferred invitation.
    pub fn decline_invitation(&mut self, invitation_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let (_, st) = self
            .inbox
            .get_mut(invitation_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("invitation not found in inbox".into()))?;
        if !matches!(st, InvitationState::Pending | InvitationState::Deferred { .. }) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation is no longer open".into()));
        }
        *st = InvitationState::Declined;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Ignore an invitation without altering state or emitting any record;
    /// silence never counts as acceptance, and expiry closes it naturally.
    pub fn ignore_invitation(&self, invitation_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        if !self.inbox.contains_key(invitation_id) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation not found in inbox".into()));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Caller cancels an unaccepted outgoing invitation.
    pub fn cancel_invitation(&mut self, invitation_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let (_, st) = self
            .outbox
            .get_mut(invitation_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("invitation not found in outbox".into()))?;
        if !matches!(st, InvitationState::Pending | InvitationState::Deferred { .. }) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation cannot be cancelled in current state".into()));
        }
        *st = InvitationState::Cancelled;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Recipient accepts a still-valid invitation, creating a `CallSession`
    /// and ensuring the shared `ConversationSpace` exists. Public-room
    /// memberships remain completely untouched.
    pub fn accept_invitation(&mut self, invitation_id: &str, now: u64) -> Result<CallSession> {
        let (inv, is_open) = {
            let (inv, st) = self
                .inbox
                .get(invitation_id)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("invitation not found in inbox".into()))?;
            (
                inv.clone(),
                matches!(st, InvitationState::Pending | InvitationState::Deferred { .. }),
            )
        };
        if !is_open {
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation is no longer open".into()));
        }
        if now > inv.expires_at {
            if let Some((_, st)) = self.inbox.get_mut(invitation_id) {
                *st = InvitationState::Expired;
            }
            return Err(Error::Policy("invitation expired".into()));
        }
        let perm = self
            .granted_permissions
            .get(&inv.permission_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("contact permission not found".into()))?;
        if perm.revoked || perm.revision != inv.permission_revision {
            if let Some((_, st)) = self.inbox.get_mut(invitation_id) {
                *st = InvitationState::Revoked;
            }
            return Err(Error::Policy("contact permission revoked or superseded".into()));
        }
        if now > perm.expires_at {
            return Err(Error::Policy("contact permission expired".into()));
        }

        let conversation_id = pair_conversation_id(&inv.caller, &inv.recipient);
        let session_id = format!("sess:{}", inv.invitation_id);
        let session = CallSession {
            session_id: session_id.clone(),
            conversation_id: conversation_id.clone(),
            invitation_id: inv.invitation_id.clone(),
            participants: [inv.caller.clone(), inv.recipient.clone()],
            status: SessionStatus::Active,
            started_at: now,
            expires_at: None,
        };

        self.sessions.insert(session_id.clone(), session.clone());
        self.conversations
            .entry(conversation_id.clone())
            .or_insert_with(|| ConversationSpace {
                conversation_id,
                participants: [inv.caller.clone(), inv.recipient.clone()],
                messages: Vec::new(),
                kept_items: Vec::new(),
            });
        if let Some((_, st)) = self.inbox.get_mut(invitation_id) {
            *st = InvitationState::Accepted { session_id };
        }
        Ok(session)
    }

    /// Caller records that the recipient accepted their outgoing invitation.
    pub fn sync_accepted_session(&mut self, session: CallSession) -> Result<()> {
        let (inv, st) = self
            .outbox
            .get_mut(&session.invitation_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("outgoing invitation not found".into()))?;
        if !matches!(st, InvitationState::Pending | InvitationState::Deferred { .. }) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("outgoing invitation is no longer pending".into()));
        }
        if !session.participants.contains(&inv.caller)
            || !session.participants.contains(&inv.recipient)
        {
            return Err(Error::Verification("session participants do not match invitation".into()));
        }
        *st = InvitationState::Accepted {
            session_id: session.session_id.clone(),
        };
        let conv_id = session.conversation_id.clone();
        let parts = session.participants.clone();
        self.sessions.insert(session.session_id.clone(), session);
        self.conversations
            .entry(conv_id.clone())
            .or_insert_with(|| ConversationSpace {
                conversation_id: conv_id,
                participants: parts,
                messages: Vec::new(),
                kept_items: Vec::new(),
            });
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn hold_session(&mut self, session_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let sess = self
            .sessions
            .get_mut(session_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("session not found".into()))?;
        if sess.status != SessionStatus::Active {
            return Err(Error::Policy("only an active session can be placed on hold".into()));
        }
        sess.status = SessionStatus::OnHold;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn resume_session(&mut self, session_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let sess = self
            .sessions
            .get_mut(session_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("session not found".into()))?;
        if sess.status != SessionStatus::OnHold {
            return Err(Error::Policy("only a held session can be resumed".into()));
        }
        sess.status = SessionStatus::Active;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Unilaterally end participation in a live session without requiring peer cooperation.
    pub fn end_session(&mut self, session_id: &str, now: u64) -> Result<()> {
        let me = self.did();
        let sess = self
            .sessions
            .get_mut(session_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("session not found".into()))?;
        if matches!(sess.status, SessionStatus::Ended { .. }) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        sess.status = SessionStatus::Ended {
            ended_by: me,
            at: now,
        };
        if self.focus == AttentionFocus::PrivateSession(session_id.to_string()) {
            self.focus = AttentionFocus::Lobby;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Send a private message bound to `session_id`. Requires `expected_focus`
    /// to match the client's current `AttentionFocus` so a stale reply cannot
    /// accidentally fire into a public room or a different private thread.
    pub fn post_private(
        &mut self,
        session_id: &str,
        expected_focus: &AttentionFocus,
        text: &str,
        now: u64,
    ) -> Result<PrivateMessage> {
        let required_focus = AttentionFocus::PrivateSession(session_id.to_string());
        if &self.focus != expected_focus || expected_focus != &required_focus {
            return Err(Error::Policy(
                "destination safety check failed: current focus does not match target session"
                    .into(),
            ));
        }
        let sess = self
            .sessions
            .get(session_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("session not found".into()))?;
        if sess.status != SessionStatus::Active {
            return Err(Error::Policy("session is not active".into()));
        }
        if let Some(exp) = sess.expires_at {
            if now > exp {
                return Err(Error::Policy("session has expired".into()));
            }
        }
        let me = self.did();
        let peer = if sess.participants[0] == me {
            sess.participants[1].clone()
        } else if sess.participants[1] == me {
            sess.participants[0].clone()
        } else {
            return Err(Error::Policy("client is not a participant in this session".into()));
        };
        let conv_id = sess.conversation_id.clone();
        let conv = self
            .conversations
            .get_mut(&conv_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("conversation space missing".into()))?;
        let seq = conv.messages.len() as u64;

        let mut msg = PrivateMessage {
            conversation_id: conv_id,
            session_id: session_id.to_string(),
            seq,
            sender: me,
            recipient: peer,
            text: text.to_string(),
            ts: now,
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = body_for_signing(&msg)?;
        let sig = self.keypair.sign(&body);
        msg.proof = ProofOrArray::single(Proof::create(&self.keypair, &sig));
        conv.messages.push(msg.clone());
        Ok(msg)
    }

    /// Receive a private message from a peer. Allowed while the session is
    /// `Active` or `OnHold`; refused once the session has `Ended`.
    pub fn receive_private(&mut self, msg: PrivateMessage) -> Result<()> {
        msg.verify()?;
        if msg.recipient != self.did() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("private message addressed to another recipient".into()));
        }
        let sess = self
            .sessions
            .get(&msg.session_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("unknown session".into()))?;
        if matches!(sess.status, SessionStatus::Ended { .. }) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("session has ended".into()));
        }
        if sess.conversation_id != msg.conversation_id {
            return Err(Error::Verification("message conversation_id mismatch".into()));
        }
        if !sess.participants.contains(&msg.sender) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("sender is not a participant in this session".into()));
        }
        let conv = self
            .conversations
            .get_mut(&msg.conversation_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("conversation space missing".into()))?;
        if conv
            .messages
            .iter()
            .any(|m| m.seq == msg.seq && m.sender == msg.sender)
        {
            return Ok(());
        }
        conv.messages.push(msg);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Save a deliberate note or shared artifact reference onto the conversation table.
    pub fn keep_in_conversation(&mut self, conversation_id: &str, note: String) -> Result<()> {
        let conv = self
            .conversations
            .get_mut(conversation_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Policy("conversation space not found".into()))?;
        conv.kept_items.push(note);
        Ok(())
    }
}

// =====================================================================
// ZERO-TRAIL TEMPORARY HANDOFF ROOM
// =====================================================================

/// The only record that survives a `TemporaryHandoff`: a signed attestation
/// that a handoff space existed at `location` during `[opened_at, closed_at]`.
/// Carries zero participant IDs, zero message counts, and zero content hashes.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct HandoffAttestation {
    pub location: String,
    pub room_key: DidKey,
    pub opened_at: u64,
    pub closed_at: u64,
    pub proof: ProofOrArray,
}

impl HandoffAttestation {
    pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.location.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(Error::Verification("handoff attestation: empty location".into()));
        }
        if self.closed_at < self.opened_at {
            return Err(Error::Verification(
                "handoff attestation: closed_at < opened_at".into(),
            ));
        }
        let body = body_for_signing(self)?;
        let proof = self
            .proof
            .find_by_method(&self.room_key)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Verification("handoff attestation: missing room proof".into()))?;
        proof.verify(&body)
    }
}

/// Clean payload retained by a recipient. Intentionally carries no room ID,
/// no sender ID, and no exchange timestamp.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct DeliveredItem {
    pub title: String,
    pub media_type: String,
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Transient in-memory handoff space (deliberately non-serializable).
/// Consumed on `close`, dropping all participant handles and unaccepted data.
pub struct TemporaryHandoff {
    location: String,
    room_kp: Keypair,
    opened_at: u64,
    expires_at: u64,
    participants: Vec<DidKey>,
    pending_item: Option<(DidKey, DeliveredItem)>,
}

impl TemporaryHandoff {
    pub fn open(location: &str, now: u64, ttl: u64) -> Result<Self> {
        if location.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("handoff location cannot be empty".into()));
        }
        if ttl == 0 {
            return Err(Error::Policy("handoff ttl must be positive".into()));
        }
        Ok(TemporaryHandoff {
            location: location.to_string(),
            room_kp: Keypair::generate(),
            opened_at: now,
            expires_at: now.saturating_add(ttl),
            participants: Vec::new(),
            pending_item: None,
        })
    }

    pub fn admit(&mut self, participant: DidKey, now: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if now > self.expires_at {
            return Err(Error::Policy("handoff room has expired".into()));
        }
        if self.participants.contains(&participant) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("participant already in handoff room".into()));
        }
        if self.participants.len() >= 2 {
            return Err(Error::Policy("handoff room is limited to two participants".into()));
        }
        self.participants.push(participant);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn offer_item(&mut self, sender: &DidKey, item: DeliveredItem, now: u64) -> Result<()> {
        if now > self.expires_at {
            return Err(Error::Policy("handoff room has expired".into()));
        }
        if !self.participants.contains(sender) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("sender is not admitted to handoff room".into()));
        }
        if self.pending_item.is_some() {
            return Err(Error::Policy("an item is already waiting in this handoff room".into()));
        }
        self.pending_item = Some((sender.clone(), item));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Recipient deliberately takes ownership of the clean `DeliveredItem`,
    /// immediately wiping it from the transient room buffer.
    pub fn accept_item(&mut self, recipient: &DidKey, now: u64) -> Result<DeliveredItem> {
        if now > self.expires_at {
            return Err(Error::Policy("handoff room has expired".into()));
        }
        if !self.participants.contains(recipient) {
            return Err(Error::Policy("recipient is not admitted to handoff room".into()));
        }
        let Some((sender, _)) = &self.pending_item else {
            return Err(Error::Policy("no item waiting in handoff room".into()));
        };
        if sender == recipient {
            return Err(Error::Policy("sender cannot accept their own offered item".into()));
        }
        let (_, item) = self.pending_item.take().unwrap();
        Ok(item)
    }

    /// Consume the temporary room, wiping all transient state and returning
    /// only the signed lifecycle attestation.
    pub fn close(self, now: u64) -> Result<HandoffAttestation> {
        if now < self.opened_at {
            return Err(Error::Policy("close time precedes open time".into()));
        }
        let mut att = HandoffAttestation {
            location: self.location,
            room_key: self.room_kp.did(),
            opened_at: self.opened_at,
            closed_at: now,
            proof: ProofOrArray::placeholder(),
        };
        let body = body_for_signing(&att)?;
        let sig = self.room_kp.sign(&body);
        att.proof = ProofOrArray::single(Proof::create(&self.room_kp, &sig));
        Ok(att)
    }
}

tests/contact.rs
use chat_world::contact::{
    AttentionFocus, ClientSnapshot, ContactMode, DeliveredItem, HandoffAttestation,
    InvitationState, ParticipantClient, SessionStatus, TemporaryHandoff,
};
use chat_world::error::Result;
use chat_world::Keypair;

#[test]
fn outing_split_defer_accept_private_call_and_restart() -> Result<()> {
    let alice_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let bob_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let music_room = Keypair::generate().did();
    let story_room = Keypair::generate().did();

    let mut alice = ParticipantClient::new(alice_kp.clone());
    let mut bob = ParticipantClient::new(bob_kp.clone());

    // 1. Both start together in Music room and exchange contact permissions.
    alice.enter_public_room(music_room.clone());
    bob.enter_public_room(music_room.clone());

    let perm_from_bob = bob.grant_contact(
        alice.did(),
        "endpoint://bob-contact-01".into(),
        vec![ContactMode::LiveCall],
        1000,
    )?;
    alice.receive_permission(perm_from_bob.clone())?;

    // 2. They separate into different rooms.
    bob.enter_public_room(story_room.clone());
    assert!(alice.public_rooms().contains(&music_room));
    assert!(bob.public_rooms().contains(&story_room));

    // 3. Alice sends a bounded invitation with a clear purpose.
    let inv = alice.send_invitation(
        &perm_from_bob.permission_id,
        ContactMode::LiveCall,
        "Found a pattern question—want to compare notes?".into(),
        100,
        200,
    )?;
    bob.receive_invitation(inv.clone(), 105)?;
    // Duplicate retry delivery does not create a second inbox item or error.
    bob.receive_invitation(inv.clone(), 106)?;

    // 4. Bob defers to finish his current story exchange.
    bob.defer_invitation(
        &inv.invitation_id,
        Some("Finishing one turn in the story room first.".into()),
        110,
    )?;
    assert!(matches!(
        bob.inbox_state(&inv.invitation_id),
        Some(InvitationState::Deferred { .. })
    ));

    // 5. Bob accepts while still valid; public-room memberships do not change.
    let session = bob.accept_invitation(&inv.invitation_id, 150)?;
    alice.sync_accepted_session(session.clone())?;
    assert!(bob.public_rooms().contains(&story_room));
    assert!(alice.public_rooms().contains(&music_room));

    // 6. Focus safety: Alice is still focused on the public music room,
    // so attempting to post privately with stale focus is refused.
    let stale_focus = AttentionFocus::PublicRoom(music_room.clone());
    assert!(alice
        .post_private(&session.session_id, &stale_focus, "should not leak", 155)
        .is_err());

    // 7. Alice switches focus explicitly to the private session and sends a message.
    let priv_focus = AttentionFocus::PrivateSession(session.session_id.clone());
    alice.set_focus(priv_focus.clone());
    let msg = alice.post_private(&session.session_id, &priv_focus, "Look at A B A C A.", 160)?;
    bob.receive_private(msg)?;
    bob.keep_in_conversation(&session.conversation_id, "Question: What can change?".into())?;

    // 8. Bob ends the call unilaterally without requiring Alice's cooperation.
    bob.end_session(&session.session_id, 200)?;
    assert!(matches!(
        bob.session(&session.session_id).unwrap().status,
        SessionStatus::Ended { .. }
    ));

    // 9. Restart recovery: snapshot to JSON, drop client, and restore.
    let snap_json = serde_json::to_string(&bob.snapshot()).unwrap();
    let parsed_snap: ClientSnapshot = serde_json::from_str(&snap_json).unwrap();
    let mut bob_restarted = ParticipantClient::restore(parsed_snap, bob_kp)?;

    assert!(matches!(
        bob_restarted.session(&session.session_id).unwrap().status,
        SessionStatus::Ended { .. }
    ));
    assert_eq!(
        bob_restarted
            .conversation(&session.conversation_id)
            .unwrap()
            .kept_items,
        vec!["Question: What can change?".to_string()]
    );

    // Messages sent to an ended session are refused after restart.
    let late_msg = alice.post_private(&session.session_id, &priv_focus, "still there?", 210)?;
    assert!(bob_restarted.receive_private(late_msg).is_err());

    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn revocation_blocks_pending_and_new_calls_while_disconnect_also_ends_active() -> Result<()> {
    let alice_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let bob_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let mut alice = ParticipantClient::new(alice_kp);
    let mut bob = ParticipantClient::new(bob_kp.clone());

    let perm = bob.grant_contact(
        alice.did(),
        "endpoint://bob-02".into(),
        vec![ContactMode::LiveCall],
        500,
    )?;
    alice.receive_permission(perm.clone())?;

    // Accept one live session first.
    let inv1 = alice.send_invitation(&perm.permission_id, ContactMode::LiveCall, "call 1".into(), 10, 100)?;
    bob.receive_invitation(inv1.clone(), 11)?;
    let sess1 = bob.accept_invitation(&inv1.invitation_id, 12)?;
    alice.sync_accepted_session(sess1.clone())?;

    // Send a second pending invitation.
    let inv2 = alice.send_invitation(&perm.permission_id, ContactMode::LiveCall, "call 2".into(), 20, 100)?;
    bob.receive_invitation(inv2.clone(), 21)?;

    // Revoking permission cancels pending inv2 and blocks acceptance,
    // but leaves already-accepted sess1 alive under its own session authorization.
    let revoked_perm = bob.revoke_permission(&perm.permission_id)?;
    assert_eq!(bob.inbox_state(&inv2.invitation_id), Some(&InvitationState::Revoked));
    assert!(bob.accept_invitation(&inv2.invitation_id, 25).is_err());
    assert_eq!(bob.session(&sess1.session_id).unwrap().status, SessionStatus::Active);

    // Anti-rollback: Alice receives the revocation, then tries to replay the older permission.
    alice.receive_permission(revoked_perm)?;
    assert!(alice.receive_permission(perm.clone()).is_err());
    assert!(alice
        .send_invitation(&perm.permission_id, ContactMode::LiveCall, "call 3".into(), 30, 100)
        .is_err());

    // Revocation survives client restart.
    let snap = bob.snapshot();
    let mut bob_restored = ParticipantClient::restore(snap, bob_kp)?;
    assert!(bob_restored.accept_invitation(&inv2.invitation_id, 35).is_err());

    // Explicit disconnect revokes and ends the active session too.
    bob_restored.disconnect(&perm.permission_id, 40)?;
    assert!(matches!(
        bob_restored.session(&sess1.session_id).unwrap().status,
        SessionStatus::Ended { .. }
    ));

    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn ignore_leaves_no_acceptance_and_mode_limits_are_enforced() -> Result<()> {
    let alice_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let bob_kp = Keypair::generate();
    let mut alice = ParticipantClient::new(alice_kp);
    let mut bob = ParticipantClient::new(bob_kp);

    let perm = bob.grant_contact(
        alice.did(),
        "endpoint://bob-03".into(),
        vec![ContactMode::LiveCall],
        500,
    )?;
    alice.receive_permission(perm.clone())?;

    // AsyncMessage is not in allowed_modes -> refused.
    assert!(alice
        .send_invitation(
            &perm.permission_id,
            ContactMode::AsyncMessage,
            "unsolicited async note".into(),
            10,
            100,
        )
        .is_err());

    // Ignoring keeps invitation pending until it expires; silence never accepts.
    let inv = alice.send_invitation(
        &perm.permission_id,
        ContactMode::LiveCall,
        "quick hello".into(),
        10,
        50,
    )?;
    bob.receive_invitation(inv.clone(), 12)?;
    bob.ignore_invitation(&inv.invitation_id)?;
    assert_eq!(bob.inbox_state(&inv.invitation_id), Some(&InvitationState::Pending));

    // Past expiry (10 + 50 = 60), acceptance fails and marks Expired.
    assert!(bob.accept_invitation(&inv.invitation_id, 61).is_err());
    assert_eq!(bob.inbox_state(&inv.invitation_id), Some(&InvitationState::Expired));

    Ok(())
}

#[test]
fn temporary_handoff_leaves_only_lifecycle_attestation_and_clean_item() -> Result<()> {
    let alice = Keypair::generate().did();
    let bob = Keypair::generate().did();
    let secret_payload = b"confidential draft constraint".to_vec();

    let mut handoff = TemporaryHandoff::open("commons/dock-04", 1000, 60)?;
    handoff.admit(alice.clone(), 1001)?;
    handoff.admit(bob.clone(), 1002)?;

    // Third participant is refused.
    let carol = Keypair::generate().did();
    assert!(handoff.admit(carol, 1003).is_err());

    handoff.offer_item(
        &alice,
        DeliveredItem {
            title: "Constraint Note".into(),
            media_type: "text/plain".into(),
            bytes: secret_payload.clone(),
        },
        1010,
    )?;

    // Sender cannot accept their own item; recipient takes it cleanly.
    assert!(handoff.accept_item(&alice, 1011).is_err());
    let received = handoff.accept_item(&bob, 1012)?;
    assert_eq!(received.bytes, secret_payload);

    // Close consumes the room and returns ONLY the signed lifecycle attestation.
    let attestation = handoff.close(1020)?;
    attestation.verify()?;

    // Verify zero participant or content leakage in the attestation JSON.
    let att_json = serde_json::to_string(&attestation).unwrap();
    assert!(!att_json.contains(alice.as_str()));
    assert!(!att_json.contains(bob.as_str()));
    assert!(!att_json.contains("Constraint Note"));
    assert!(!att_json.contains("confidential"));

    // Verify zero exchange provenance leakage in the retained item JSON.
    let item_json = serde_json::to_string(&received).unwrap();
    assert!(!item_json.contains(alice.as_str()));
    assert!(!item_json.contains(bob.as_str()));
    assert!(!item_json.contains(attestation.room_key.as_str()));
    assert!(!item_json.contains("commons/dock-04"));

    // Attestation rejects unknown injected fields (e.g. a leaked roster).
    let mut bad_att = serde_json::to_value(&attestation).unwrap();
    bad_att["participants"] = serde_json::json!([alice.as_str(), bob.as_str()]);
    assert!(serde_json::from_value::<HandoffAttestation>(bad_att).is_err());

    Ok(())
}
